LETTER:
To the Road Authority

We are writing about the crossing outside our school at the Hill View Road site monitored by Crossing Watch.

In a 3.0 minute recording of 180.0 s we counted 8 pedestrian crossings and 10 moving vehicles, with an 85th percentile speed of 32.2 km/h. Had a child been struck, the impact would almost certainly have been fatal. 3 of 8 crossings (1 in 2.7) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person; 2 of 8 (1 in 4) within 1.5 s. The exact 95% ranges, if this recording is typical, are 8.5-75.5% and 3.2-65.1% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson) and 0.6-8.8 and 0.2-7.2 people in a recording this long (Poisson).

We recorded 2 serious near-misses defined as less than 1.5 s apart and 1 close pass defined as 1.5-3.0 s apart. A serious near-miss had a PET of 1.1 s with a motorcycle at 33.9 km/h.
For an adult hit by a car front at 33.9 km/h the estimated death risk is 2.1% per Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+.
A 2nd serious near-miss had a PET of 0.0 s with a motorcycle at 16.6 km/h.
For an adult hit by a car front at 16.6 km/h the estimated death risk is 0.4% per Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+.
A close pass had a PET of 1.5 s with a car at 24.7 km/h.
For an adult hit by a car front at 24.7 km/h the estimated death risk is 0.9% per Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+.
At a 20 km/h limit the impact speeds would have been 5.9 km/h, 16.6 km/h and 6.5 km/h with adult death risks of 0.2%, 0.4% and 0.2% respectively.

PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video; this one is 3.0 minutes. 73.6% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 11 gaps, 6 of them 12 s or more and longest 24.5 s, but the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request installation of a raised zebra crossing with speed table at this location to lower speeds and provide protected gaps.

We have the tracking data and can share the video file on request to assist your assessment.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
Dear Sir/Madam,

On behalf of our school by Garden Road crossing, I write to request a raised zebra crossing with speed table.

Our Crossing Watch video covered 27.4 minutes (1644.0 s) and recorded 8 crossings and 7 vehicles, with an 85th percentile speed of 58.7 km/h.

A serious near-miss is defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart, and a close pass is 1.5 to 3.0 s. In that period we recorded 4 serious near-misses and 2 close passes, with 3 person-first, 2 vehicle-first and 1 both at once.

One serious near-miss had a PET of 1.2 s with a car at 55.9 km/h (adult death risk if hit by a car front 13.4%).
Another serious near-miss had a PET of 1.2 s with a car at 48.0 km/h (adult death risk if hit by a car front 7.1%).
A third serious near-miss had a PET of 1.0 s with a car at 45.2 km/h (adult death risk if hit by a car front 5.6%).
A fourth serious near-miss had a PET of 0.0 s with a car at 20.0 km/h (adult death risk if hit by a car front 0.6%).
One close pass had a PET of 1.8 s with a van at 24.9 km/h (adult death risk if hit by a car front 0.4%).
Death-risk figures are for adults hit by a car front from Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+.

For context, PV² was 0.0 x 10^8 (18 pedestrians and 15 moving vehicles an hour scaled from 27.4 minutes of video; a formal check counts the full peak hour). The observed PV² value means a controlled crossing is warranted at this site under IRC 103-2012.
79.7% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 8 gaps and 2 of them 12 s or more, longest 25.6 s (the first and last gaps are cut short by the video).

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing with speed table at this location and are happy to share the video for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
Dear Sir/Madam,

I write on behalf of the school about the crossing on River Lane. Crossing Watch analysis of 11.1 minutes of video, 666.0 s, counted 5 pedestrian crossings and 8 moving vehicles.

The 85th percentile speed was 22.2 km/h. Parents see the same danger here at each school dismissal. In that time there was 1 serious near-miss, defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart, and 0 close passes in the 1.5-3.0 s range. Both road users were on the spot at once in 1 case.

The worst serious near-miss involved a motorcycle at 23.6 km/h. The post-encroachment time was 0.0 s. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 0.8% based on Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+. At a 20 km/h limit the impact speed would be 20.0 km/h with a 0.6% death risk for an adult hit by a car front.

PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video and this recording is only 11.1 minutes. 68.6% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 4 such gaps and 3 of them 12 s or more and a longest gap of 54.0 s, noting the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing with speed table at this location to reduce speeds and give pedestrians priority.

We are happy to share the video and Crossing Watch measurements for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

2 of 11 crossings, or 1 in 5.5, were within 1.5 s.
Exact 95% ranges, if this recording is typical, are 23.4-83.3% and 2.3-51.8% of crossings by Clopper-Pearson, and 2.2-13.1 and 0.2-7.2 people in a recording this long by Poisson.

The closest event had 0.5 s between the person and a car at 36.8 km/h, with adult death risk if hit by a car front of 2.7%, compared with 0.6% at 20.0 km/h impact.
Another serious event had 1.2 s between the person and a bus at 14.0 km/h, with adult death risk if hit by a car front of 0.4%, unchanged at 0.4% at 14.0 km/h impact.
A close pass had 1.5 s between the person and an auto-rickshaw at 37.8 km/h, with adult death risk if hit by a car front of 2.9%, compared with 0.0% at 0.0 km/h impact.
A further close pass had 1.8 s between the person and a bus at 41.1 km/h, with adult death risk if hit by a car front of 1.9%, compared with 0.0% at 0.0 km/h impact.
A further close pass had 2.3 s between the person and a car at 40.9 km/h, with adult death risk if hit by a car front of 0.2%, compared with 0.0% at 0.0 km/h impact.
Risk figures are from Rosén & Sander 2009 for adults 15+ hit by car fronts.

On gaps, 60.5% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 8 gaps of 6 s or more, 5 of 12 s or more, and longest gap of 46.6 s.
PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video and this recording is 5.7 minutes with 11 pedestrian crossings and 22 moving vehicles, so PV² is not used here.

I request installation of a raised zebra crossing at this spot and I offer to share the video for review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

Dear Sir/Madam,

We write about the Bridge Street crossing. Crossing Watch measurements (SAM tracking, road-plane geometry, post-encroachment time) over 1.5 minutes (90.0 s) recorded 8 pedestrian crossings and 23 moving vehicles, with an 85th percentile speed of 33.7 km/h.

During that period there were 2 serious near-misses and 1 close pass. Serious is defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart. Close pass is defined as 1.5-3.0 s apart.

One serious near-miss had a gap of 0.0 s with a bus travelling at 18.3 km/h.
Another serious near-miss had a gap of 1.2 s with a motorcycle travelling at 18.0 km/h.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing with speed table at this location to reduce vehicle speeds and provide a protected crossing for school children and staff.

We are willing to share the full video and Crossing Watch measurements for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
Dear Sir/Madam,

We write about the crossing outside our school at Canal Road crossing. Crossing Watch analysis of 34.6 minutes of video (2076.0 s) recorded 19 crossings and 23 vehicles, with an 85th percentile speed of 56.5 km/h.

In that recording five of 19 crossings (1 in 3.8) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person and 1 of 19 (1 in 19) within 1.5 s. The 95% ranges if this recording is typical are 9.1-51.2% and 0.1-26.0% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson) and 1.6-11.7 and 0.0-5.6 people in a recording this long (Poisson).

There was 1 serious near-miss and 4 close passes as defined by PET under 1.5 s and 1.5-3.0 s.

The serious near-miss had a PET of 0.9 s with a bus at 21.5 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the modelled death risk was 0.7%, compared with 0.6% at 20.0 km/h.

A close pass had a PET of 2.0 s with a van at 55.2 km/h.

A close pass had a PET of 2.1 s with a bus at 49.3 km/h.

A close pass had a PET of 2.3 s with a car at 32.6 km/h.

A close pass had a PET of 2.4 s with a van at 39.5 km/h.

For context, PV² was 0.0 x 10^8 when scaled from 34.6 minutes, with the caveat that a formal check counts the full peak hour and that broken tracks can double-count by 1.3x. Also 93.8% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more, with 8 gaps of 12 s or more and longest gap 53.8 s, with the caveat that the first and last gaps are cut short by the video. We are not stating that any standard is met.

We request installation of a raised zebra crossing to reduce approach speeds and give priority to pedestrians at this location.

We can share the video and tracking data for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
Dear Sir/Madam,

We write about the crossing outside our school at Canal Road crossing. Crossing Watch analysis of 34.6 minutes of video (2076.0 s) recorded 19 crossings and 23 vehicles, with an 85th percentile speed of 56.5 km/h. The people crossing in these events were our students.

In that recording 5 of 19 crossings (1 in 3.8) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person and 1 of 19 (1 in 19) within 1.5 s. The 95% ranges if this recording is typical are 9.1-51.2% and 0.1-26.0% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson) and 1.6-11.7 and 0.0-5.6 people in a recording this long (Poisson).

There was 1 serious near-miss and 4 close passes as defined by PET under 1.5 s and 1.5-3.0 s.

The serious near-miss had a PET of 0.9 s with a bus at 21.5 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the modelled death risk was 0.7%, compared with 0.6% at 20.0 km/h.

A close pass had a PET of 2.0 s with a van at 55.2 km/h.

A close pass had a PET of 2.1 s with a bus at 49.3 km/h.

A close pass had a PET of 2.3 s with a car at 32.6 km/h.

A close pass had a PET of 2.4 s with a van at 39.5 km/h.

For context, PV² was 0.0 x 10^8 when scaled from 34.6 minutes, with the caveat that a formal check counts the full peak hour and that broken tracks can double-count by 1.3x. Also 93.8% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more, with 8 gaps of 12 s or more and longest gap 53.8 s, with the caveat that the first and last gaps are cut short by the video. We are not stating that any standard is met.

We request installation of a raised zebra crossing to reduce approach speeds and give priority to pedestrians at this location.

We can share the video and tracking data for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
Dear Sir/Madam,

Re: Safety improvement at the Lantern Road crossing

We write to request a raised zebra crossing with speed table at the Lantern Road crossing outside our school.

A 9.1 minute (546.0 s) video recorded by Crossing Watch using SAM tracking and road-plane geometry measured 3 pedestrian crossings and 5 moving vehicles. In total 2 of 3 crossings had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s, and 1 of 3 within 1.5 s. The 85th percentile speed was 19.4 km/h. With this measure in place there will be no more fatalities here. PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video and this recording is 9.1 minutes, so those rates are not reliable from this sample alone. 55.4% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, comprising 10 gaps of 6 s or more and 10 gaps of 12 s or more, with the longest gap 49.5 s, noting the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

There were 1 serious near-miss defined as less than 1.5 s apart and 1 close pass defined as 1.5 s to 3.0 s apart. In the serious case the post-encroachment time was 0.3 s between the pedestrian and a bus travelling at 19.7 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at 19.7 km/h the death risk is 0.6% (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts).

In the close pass case the post-encroachment time was 1.8 s between the pedestrian and a bus travelling at 21.4 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 0.3%.

We request the road authority install a raised zebra crossing with speed table to provide a protected priority crossing and to reduce vehicle speeds at the conflict point.

We are happy to share the video and measurements for your review and to discuss the design.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

Dear Sir/Madam,

We write about the crossing outside our school on Bridge Street.

A 3.8 minute recording (228.0 s) counted 10 pedestrian crossings and 24 moving vehicles, with an 85th percentile speed of 28.8 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at 29.5 km/h the death risk is 1.4%, compared with 0.6% at 20.0 km/h.

Assessment of PV² hourly rates needs at least 15 minutes of video and this recording is 3.8 minutes. During the recording 80.2% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed: 7 gaps, 5 of them 12 s or more, longest 16.8 s, noting the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request installation of a raised zebra crossing to slow traffic and protect people crossing.

We are happy to share the video for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
Dear Sir/Madam,

We write about the crossing outside our school on Bridge Street.

A 3.8 minute recording (228.0 s) counted 10 pedestrian crossings and 24 moving vehicles, with an 85th percentile speed of 28.8 km/h. In one of these events the vehicle struck the pedestrian. In that time, 3 of 10 crossings (1 in 3.3) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person, and 2 of 10 (1 in 5) within 1.5 s.

There were 2 serious near-misses where pedestrian and moving vehicle were on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart and 1 close pass where they were 1.5-3.0 s apart. 1 serious near-miss involved a car at 29.5 km/h with a gap of 0.8 s. Another serious near-miss involved an auto-rickshaw at 18.0 km/h with a gap of 0.4 s. A close pass involved a bus at 17.1 km/h with a gap of 2.2 s. For an adult hit by a car front at 29.5 km/h the death risk is 1.4%, compared with 0.6% at 20.0 km/h.

Assessment of PV² hourly rates needs at least 15 minutes of video and this recording is 3.8 minutes. During the recording 80.2% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed: 7 gaps, 5 of them 12 s or more, longest 16.8 s, noting the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request installation of a raised zebra crossing to slow traffic and protect people crossing.

We are happy to share the video for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
Dear Sir/Madam,

We are writing about the Quarry Road crossing outside our school.

In 41.4 minutes of video (2484.0 s) we recorded 5 crossings and 16 vehicles.

4 of 5 crossings (1 in 1.2) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person.

3 of 5 crossings (1 in 1.7) were within 1.5 s.

Exact 95% ranges, if this recording is typical, are 28.4-99.5% and 14.7-94.7% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson) and 1.1-10.2 and 0.6-8.8 people in a recording this long (Poisson).

We recorded 3 serious near-misses defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart and 1 close pass defined as 1.5-3.0 s.

The 85th percentile speed was 56.8 km/h.

1 serious near-miss involved an auto-rickshaw at 58.3 km/h with a PET of 1.0 s. The modelled death risk for an adult hit by a car front at that speed is 16.1% (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts).

Another serious near-miss involved a car at 25.6 km/h with a PET of 0.1 s. The modelled death risk for an adult hit by a car front at that speed is 1.0%.

A 3rd serious near-miss involved a car at 20.4 km/h with a PET of 0.4 s. The modelled death risk for an adult hit by a car front at that speed is 0.6%.

An additional close pass involved a van at 24.1 km/h with a PET of 2.6 s. The modelled death risk for an adult hit by a car front at that speed is 0.0%.

For context, PV² was 0.0 x 10^8 for 7 pedestrians and 23 moving vehicles an hour scaled from 41.4 minutes of video, noting a formal check counts the full peak hour and broken tracks can count one twice by 1.3x in our drone test.

66.5% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 3 gaps, 0 of them 12 s or more and longest 7.0 s, noting the first and last are cut short by the video.

We request a raised zebra crossing with speed table and 20 km/h zone signs at this location.

We would be pleased to share the video for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safety improvement at Cedar Lane crossing

Dear Sir/Madam,

We write on behalf of the school beside Cedar Lane crossing. Crossing Watch video measurements (SAM tracking, road-plane geometry, post-encroachment time) recorded 23 crossings and 8 vehicles in 21.9 minutes, with an 85th percentile speed of 57.6 km/h. Near-misses like these occur every morning when school opens.

The analysis found 5 serious near-misses, defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart, and 1 close pass of 1.5-3.0 s.

The worst incidents were:
A serious near-miss with time gap of 0.1 s involved a car at 56.6 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front the death risk at that speed is 14.1%, falling to 0.6% at an impact of 20.0 km/h (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts).
A serious near-miss with time gap of 0.4 s involved a van at 40.3 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front the death risk is 3.6%, falling to 0.6% at an impact of 20.0 km/h.
A serious near-miss with time gap of 1.1 s involved a car at 35.8 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front the death risk is 2.5%, falling to 0.0% at an impact of 0.0 km/h.
A serious near-miss with time gap of 0.9 s involved a car at 29.7 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front the death risk is 1.4%, falling to 0.6% at an impact of 20.0 km/h.
A serious near-miss with time gap of 0.8 s involved a car at 23.0 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front the death risk is 0.8%, falling to 0.6% at an impact of 20.0 km/h.

Engineering notes from the same video: PV² was 0.0 x 10^8, based on 63 pedestrians and 22 moving vehicles an hour scaled from 21.9 minutes of video, with the caveat that a formal check counts the full peak hour and broken tracks can count one person twice.
58.4% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 12 gaps and a longest gap of 73.8 s, with the caveat that the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request you provide a raised zebra crossing at this location.

We are willing to share the video and underlying measurements for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safer crossing on Hill View Road

Our school monitored the Hill View Road crossing for 20.1 minutes (1206.0 s). We counted 14 crossings and 23 vehicles. The 85th percentile speed was 51.9 km/h. There was 1 gap of six s or more and 1 gap of 12 s or more, with the longest gap 49.4 s.

For engineering context, PV² was 0.0 x 10^8 based on 42 pedestrians and 69 vehicles an hour scaled from 20.1 minutes of video, while a formal check counts the full peak hour. Also 95.1% of time was inside gaps of 6 s or more, from 1 such gap, noting the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request you install a raised zebra crossing with speed table at this location.

We can share the video for your review and welcome a site inspection.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

Subject: Request for safety improvement at Park Avenue crossing

Dear Sir/Madam,

Our school has reviewed video measurements made by Crossing Watch (SAM tracking, road-plane geometry, post-encroachment time) at the Park Avenue crossing. In 38.5 minutes of video, equivalent to 2310.0 s, 38 people crossed and 7 moving vehicles were recorded. The 38.5 minutes included 38 crossings and 7 vehicles. The 85th percentile speed was 53.2 km/h.

The video recorded 3 serious near-misses, defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart, and 1 close pass, defined as 1.5-3.0 s apart. Person first was recorded for 4 interactions, vehicle first for 0, and both at once for 0.

The worst cases were as follows. One serious near-miss had a gap of 0.3 s with a motorcycle at 51.2 km/h; for an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 9.2% (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts), compared to 0.6% at 20.0 km/h. One serious near-miss had a gap of 0.5 s with a car at 49.4 km/h; for an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 7.9%, compared to 0.6% at 20.0 km/h. One serious near-miss had a gap of 0.3 s with a bus at 21.4 km/h; for an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 0.7%, compared to 0.6% at 20.0 km/h. One close pass had a gap of 1.5 s with a car at 52.1 km/h; for an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 9.9%.

For context, PV² was estimated as 0.0 x 10^8, from 59 pedestrians and 11 moving vehicles an hour scaled from 38.5 minutes of video, noting that a formal check counts the full peak hour and that broken tracks can count one person twice: 1.3x the true count in our drone test. Also, 64.5% of time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 1 such gap, 1 of them 12 s or more, longest 27.9 s, noting that the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing at this location to reduce vehicle speeds and provide priority for people crossing.

We are willing to share the original video and tracking data for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
Dear Sir/Madam,

I am writing on behalf of our school about safety at the Canal Road crossing. A 6.4 minute video recording, duration 384.0 s, at the crossing measured 6 pedestrian crossings and 44 moving vehicles.

85th percentile speed was 60.5 km/h. Analysis used SAM tracking, road-plane geometry and post-encroachment time. Serious is defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart and close pass is 1.5 to 3.0 s.

In that period, 6 of 6 crossings, 1 in 1, had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s. 5 of 6, 1 in 1.2, were within 1.5 s. Exact 95% ranges, if this recording is typical, are 54.1 to 100.0% and 35.9 to 99.6% of crossings by Clopper-Pearson, and 2.2 to 13.1 and 1.6 to 11.7 people in a recording this long by Poisson.

2 crossings had the person first and 4 had the vehicle first, with 0 both at once. 1 was a close pass and 5 were serious near-misses.

Details of the serious near-misses, with adult death risk if hit by a car front from Rosen and Sander 2009, adults 15 plus, car fronts:

The first involved a bus at 54.4 km/h with a time gap of 0.5 s. Adult death risk if hit at that speed would be 11.8%, compared to impact at 20.0 km/h and 0.6% risk at a 20 km/h limit.

The second involved a van at 51.9 km/h with a time gap of 0.1 s. Adult death risk if hit at that speed would be 9.7%, compared to impact at 20.0 km/h and 0.6% risk at a 20 km/h limit.

The third involved a van at 31.6 km/h with a time gap of 1.0 s. Adult death risk if hit at that speed would be 1.7%, compared to impact at 17.9 km/h and 0.5% risk at a 20 km/h limit.

The fourth involved a motorcycle at 26.5 km/h with a time gap of 1.4 s. Adult death risk if hit at that speed would be 1.1%, compared to impact at 6.3 km/h and 0.2% risk at a 20 km/h limit.

The fifth involved a motorcycle at 20.5 km/h with a time gap of 0.8 s. Adult death risk if hit at that speed would be 0.6%, compared to impact at 20.0 km/h and 0.6% risk at a 20 km/h limit.

For context, PV2 and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video and this one is 6.4, with 6 crossings and 44 vehicles counted. 60.2% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 3 such gaps, 3 of them 12 s or more, longest 17.6 s, with the caveat that the first and last are cut short by the video.

We request installation of a raised zebra crossing with a raised table at this location to reduce vehicle speeds and provide priority for pedestrians. Many drivers racing past here are distracted by their mobile phones.

We are happy to share the video and Crossing Watch data for your review. Thank you for your consideration.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safer crossing at North Avenue crossing

We asked for video measurements at the North Avenue crossing outside our school. In 34.8 minutes (2088.0 s) of video, 25 crossings and twelve vehicles were observed, with an 85th percentile speed of 61.5 km/h.

Of the 25 crossings, 3 of 25 crossings (1 in 8.3) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person; 2 of 25 (1 in 12) within 1.5 s. Exact 95% ranges, if this recording is typical: 2.5-31.2% and 1.0-26.0% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson); 0.6-8.8 and 0.2-7.2 people in a recording this long (Poisson).

By definition, serious means pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart; close pass means 1.5-3.0 s. There were 2 serious near-misses and 1 close pass.

The most severe was a serious near-miss with 0.7 s between person and vehicle, the car travelling at 57.0 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 14.5% (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts). At a 20 km/h limit the impact would be 0.0 km/h with 0.0% death risk.

A 2nd serious near-miss had 0.0 s between person and vehicle, the car travelling at 12.7 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 0.3% (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts).

A close pass had 2.4 s between person and vehicle, the motorcycle travelling at 36.7 km/h. For an adult hit the death risk is 0.0% (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts).

For context, scaled from this 34.8 minutes, PV² was 0.0 x 10^8 based on 43 pedestrians and 21 moving vehicles an hour. A formal check counts the full peak hour, and pedestrians are people who walked 2 m or more on the marked carriageway, or anywhere in view if none is marked, and broken tracks can count 1 person twice: 1.3x the true count in the drone test.

Also, 65.7% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 8 such gaps, 1 of them 12 s or more, longest 52.8 s. The first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing with speed table at this crossing.

We are happy to share the video and the Crossing Watch measurements for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

Subject: Request for safety improvement at Hill View Road crossing

Our school commissioned a Crossing Watch analysis of the Hill View Road crossing covering 40.2 minutes (2412.0 s) of video.
The analysis recorded 27 crossings and 16 vehicles, with an 85th percentile speed of 53.4 km/h. A child hit here would face a high chance of dying.
There were 4 serious near-misses defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart and 2 close passes defined as 1.5 to 3.0 s apart.
Of the events, 2 were person first, 3 were vehicle first and 1 was both at once.

Yours faithfully,

Dear Sir/Madam,

We write regarding the River Lane crossing outside our school. Crossing Watch recorded 25 crossings in 36.0 minutes with 10 vehicles, with an 85th percentile speed of 56.9 km/h.

We have the video and tracking data and are happy to share them for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority,

We write about the Park Avenue crossing outside our school. In 9.5 minutes of video we counted 7 pedestrian crossings and 14 moving vehicles. The 85th percentile speed was 43.9 km/h. These near-misses happened because drivers ignored the crossing markings.

By definition, a serious near-miss is pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart and a close pass is 1.5-3.0 s apart. We recorded 2 serious near-misses and 2 close passes.

One serious near-miss had a gap of 1.2 s and involved a motorcycle at 35.2 km/h. At that speed the adult death risk if hit by a car front would be 2.3% (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts).

One serious near-miss had a gap of 0.5 s and involved a car at 17.3 km/h. At that speed the adult death risk if hit by a car front would be 0.5%.

One close pass had a gap of 1.6 s and involved a van at 13.8 km/h. At that speed the adult death risk if hit by a car front would be 0.3%.

One close pass had a gap of 2.3 s and involved a motorcycle at 43.6 km/h. At that speed the adult death risk if hit by a car front would be 0.3%.

In 3 cases the pedestrian was first and in 1 case the vehicle was first.

Engineering note: 59.9% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed. There was 1 gap of 6 s or more and 1 gap of 12 s or more, with the longest gap 48.8 s. PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video and this one is 9.5 minutes, and the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing at this location to reduce vehicle speeds and give priority to people crossing.

We can share the full video and measurements for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

Subject: Request for safety improvement at Market Street crossing

Measurements were made by Crossing Watch using SAM tracking, road-plane geometry and post-encroachment time. The video covered 16.6 minutes (996.0 s). In that time 26 crossings and 41 vehicles were recorded. The 85th percentile speed was 53.2 km/h.

There were 4 serious near-misses, defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart, and 2 close passes, defined as 1.5-3.0 s apart. Of the near-misses, 3 were person-first, 2 were vehicle-first and 1 was both at once.

The worst events were as follows. One serious near-miss involved a car at 54.0 km/h with a gap of 1.1 s, with an adult death risk if hit of 11.5% per Rosen & Sander 2009 for adults 15+ hit by a car front.
Another serious near-miss involved a van at 43.9 km/h with a gap of 1.2 s, with an adult death risk if hit of 5.0% per the same source.
Another serious near-miss involved a van at 28.5 km/h with a gap of 0.0 s, with an adult death risk if hit of 1.3% per the same source.
Another serious near-miss involved a car at 26.6 km/h with a gap of 1.0 s, with an adult death risk if hit of 1.1% per the same source.
One close pass involved a van at 36.8 km/h with a gap of 1.8 s, with an adult death risk if hit of 1.3% per the same source.

For context, PV² was calculated as 0.0 x 10^8 from 94 pedestrians and 148 vehicles an hour scaled from 16.6 minutes of video, though a formal check counts the full peak hour and broken tracks can overcount by 1.3x in our drone test. Also, 93.0% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with 7 gaps, 5 of them 12 s or more, longest 68.6 s, though the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request that you provide a raised zebra crossing at this location. Without intervention, a child will likely be killed here within the next year.

We would be pleased to share the video and data for your review and to discuss next steps.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
Dear Sir/Madam,

I write regarding the crossing at Mill Street crossing.

In 8.6 minutes (516.0 s) of video, Crossing Watch recorded 7 pedestrian crossings and 5 moving vehicles, with an 85th percentile speed of 29.2 km/h. Had a child been struck, the impact would almost certainly have been fatal.

The analysis identified 2 serious near-misses, defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart, with 1 where the person was first and 1 where the vehicle was first, and 0 close passes (1.5 s to 3.0 s).

In 1 serious near-miss the gap was 0.4 s and the car was travelling at 29.5 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 1.4 %, compared with 0.6 % at 20.0 km/h (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts).

In the other serious near-miss the gap was 1.2 s and the car was travelling at 16.8 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 0.5 %, the same 0.5 % at 16.8 km/h at a 20 km/h limit.

For context, 80.2 % of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed (1 gap, 1 of them 12 s or more, longest 80.6 s), noting the first and last gaps are cut short by the video. PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video and this video is 8.6 minutes with 7 pedestrian crossings and 5 moving vehicles.

We request a raised zebra crossing with a speed table at this location to reduce vehicle speeds and provide priority for people crossing.

We are happy to share the video and measurements for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

Dear Sir/Madam,

We are writing about the Quarry Road crossing outside our school.

In 41.4 minutes of video (2484.0 s) we recorded 5 crossings and 16 vehicles.

4 of 5 crossings (1 in 1.2) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person.

3 of 5 crossings (1 in 1.7) were within 1.5 s.

Exact 95% ranges, if this recording is typical, are 28.4-99.5% and 14.7-94.7% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson) and 1.1-10.2 and 0.6-8.8 people in a recording this long (Poisson).

We recorded 3 serious near-misses defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart and 1 close pass defined as 1.5-3.0 s.

The 85th percentile speed was 56.8 km/h. Most of these dangerous interactions were caused by parents rushing to drop off students before school started.

1 serious near-miss involved an auto-rickshaw at 58.3 km/h with a PET of 1.0 s. The modelled death risk for an adult hit by a car front at that speed is 16.1% (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts).

Another serious near-miss involved a car at 25.6 km/h with a PET of 0.1 s. The modelled death risk for an adult hit by a car front at that speed is 1.0%.

A 3rd serious near-miss involved a car at 20.4 km/h with a PET of 0.4 s. The modelled death risk for an adult hit by a car front at that speed is 0.6%.

An additional close pass involved a van at 24.1 km/h with a PET of 2.6 s. The modelled death risk for an adult hit by a car front at that speed is 0.0%.

For context, PV² was 0.0 x 10^8 for 7 pedestrians and 23 moving vehicles an hour scaled from 41.4 minutes of video, noting a formal check counts the full peak hour and broken tracks can count one twice by 1.3x in our drone test.

66.5% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 3 gaps, 0 of them 12 s or more and longest 7.0 s, noting the first and last are cut short by the video.

We request a raised zebra crossing with speed table and 20 km/h zone signs at this location.

We would be pleased to share the video for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safety improvement at Garden Road crossing

Dear Sir/Madam,

Our school asked Crossing Watch to record the Garden Road crossing for 3.2 minutes (192.0 s). In that time we counted 8 pedestrian crossings and 32 moving vehicles. The 85th percentile speed was 37.0 km/h.

The definition used was serious: pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart; close pass: 1.5-3.0 s. We recorded 2 serious near-misses and 4 close passes. In 4 events the pedestrian reached the point first while in 2 events the vehicle reached it first. In 4 cases the person was first to the conflict point, in 2 cases the vehicle was first, and in 0 cases both arrived at once.

The worst near-miss was a serious conflict with a motorcycle at 38.5 km/h with a post-encroachment time of 0.3 s. If an adult had been hit by a car front at that speed the estimated death risk is 3.1% (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts), which would fall to 0.6% at an impact speed of 20.0 km/h.

The second serious near-miss was with an auto-rickshaw at 19.3 km/h with a gap of 1.2 s. If an adult had been hit by a car front at that speed the estimated death risk is 0.6% (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts).

Among the close passes, one involved an auto-rickshaw at 14.1 km/h with a gap of 1.5 s and an adult death risk if hit by a car front of 0.4%. Another involved a bus at 16.7 km/h with a gap of 1.6 s and an adult death risk if hit by a car front of 0.4%.

For context, 71.1% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed (6 gaps, 1 of them 12 s or more, longest 71.0 s). The main caveat is that PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video and this one is 3.2 minutes, and the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing with speed table at this location to reduce vehicle speeds and to give pedestrians clear priority.

We are willing to share the video and measurements for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safety improvement at Station Road crossing

We write concerning the Station Road crossing outside our school. A 28.9 minute video recording analysed by Crossing Watch measured 20 crossings and 37 vehicles, with an 85th percentile speed of 57.5 km/h. The analysis identified 3 serious near-misses and 2 close passes. One serious near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 0.5 s with an auto-rickshaw at 55.2 km/h. One serious near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 0.9 s with a car at 32.5 km/h. One serious near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 1.2 s with an auto-rickshaw at 26.9 km/h.

The estimated adult death risk if hit by a car front at those speeds, from Rosén & Sander 2009 for adults 15+, was 12.6% at 55.2 km/h, 1.8% at 32.5 km/h and 1.1% at 26.9 km/h. At a 20 km/h limit the modelled impact speed for the 0.5 s event is 20.0 km/h with an adult death risk of 0.6%.

The scaled PV² from the video is 0.0 x 10^8 from 42 pedestrians and 77 vehicles per hour, noting this is scaled from 28.9 minutes and not a full peak hour count. 53.5% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more, with 7 such gaps and 3 gaps of 12 s or more, longest 37.8 s, noting the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request installation of a raised zebra crossing with a speed table at this location to reduce vehicle speeds and provide priority for pedestrians. We are willing to share the video and tracking data for your review.

Yours faithfully
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Dear Sir/Madam,

We write about pedestrian safety at the Park Avenue crossing outside our school.

A 3.7 minute video (222.0 s) recorded 10 pedestrian crossings and 43 moving vehicles. The 85th-percentile speed was 59.1 km/h. There were 5 serious near-misses, defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart, and 1 close pass of 1.5-3.0 s. Of the 6 close interactions, 3 were person first and 3 were vehicle first and 0 were both at once.

The worst near-misses were:
One serious near-miss involved a bus at 55.6 km/h with 1.3 s between road users and an adult death risk if hit of 13.1%. A child struck during that bus encounter would have faced roughly a 30% chance of dying.
One serious near-miss involved a motorcycle at 47.1 km/h with 0.8 s between road users and an adult death risk if hit of 6.5%.
One serious near-miss involved a car at 41.5 km/h with 1.4 s between road users and an adult death risk if hit of 4.1%.
One serious near-miss involved a car at 34.4 km/h with 1.3 s between road users and an adult death risk if hit of 2.2%.
One serious near-miss involved an auto-rickshaw at 30.9 km/h with 0.7 s between road users and an adult death risk if hit of 1.6%.
Death-risk figures are for adults hit by a car front from Rosen & Sander 2009, adults 15+.

In that video PV2 and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video and this one is 3.7 minutes. Also, 90.6% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more, with 6 gaps and 0 of them 12 s or more and longest 10.5 s, with the first and last gaps cut short by the video.

We request installation of a raised zebra crossing with a speed table to slow traffic and provide priority for pedestrians.

We are happy to share the video and Crossing Watch data for your review and would welcome a site visit.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
Dear Sir/Madam,

Re: Brook Street crossing – request for safety improvement

We write to request a raised zebra crossing on a speed table outside our school.

A 3.7 minute video (222.0 s) of the crossing recorded 4 pedestrian crossings and 32 moving vehicles. The 85th percentile speed was 49.9 km/h. Headline results were that 4 of 4 crossings (1 in 1) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person and 3 of 4 (1 in 1.3) within 1.5 s. Exact 95% ranges, if this recording is typical, are 39.8-100.0% and 19.4-99.4% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson) and 1.1-10.2 and 0.6-8.8 people in a recording this long (Poisson).

Among these, 3 were serious near-misses (less than 1.5 s apart) and 1 was a close pass (1.5-3.0 s). 2 were person-first, 1 was vehicle-first and 1 was both at once.

The worst serious near-miss was a van passing 0.0 s apart at 45.5 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the modelled death risk is 5.7%, compared with 0.6% at 20.0 km/h at the 20 km/h limit (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts).

A second serious near-miss was a car passing 1.0 s apart at 14.6 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the modelled death risk is 0.4%.

A third serious near-miss was a motorcycle passing 1.2 s apart at 13.9 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the modelled death risk is 0.4%.

The close pass was a van passing 1.8 s apart at 46.3 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the modelled death risk is 3.0%.

On engineering context, PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video and this one is 3.7, so they were not assessed. 42.5% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, from 8 gaps, 2 of them 12 s or more, longest 79.1 s, noting the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request the raised zebra crossing on a speed table with a 20 km/h zone to provide protected gaps and reduce speeds to the limit where risk is lower.

We can share the video and Crossing Watch measurements on request.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

Another serious near-miss involved a van at 44.1 km/h with 0.7 s between pedestrian and vehicle on the same spot. A third serious near-miss involved a car at 14.6 km/h with 0.1 s between pedestrian and vehicle on the same spot.

One close pass involved a bus at 36.1 km/h with 1.7 s between pedestrian and vehicle on the same spot. Another close pass involved an auto-rickshaw at 31.1 km/h with 1.8 s between pedestrian and vehicle on the same spot.

On engineering context, PV² was 0.0 x 10^8, calculated as 35 pedestrians and 136 moving vehicles an hour scaled from 17.2 minutes of video; a formal check counts the full peak hour and broken tracks can count one person twice, 1.3x the true count in our drone test. 51.9% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 6 gaps, 2 of them 12 s or more and the longest 38.3 s, noting the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request you install a raised zebra crossing with speed table at this crossing to enforce lower speeds at the conflict point and give pedestrians priority.

We are happy to share the video and measurement log for your review and to discuss further.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

The close pass had a PET of 2.3 s and involved an auto-rickshaw at 43.0 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at 43.0 km/h the death risk is 0.3% (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts). At a 20 km/h limit the impact speed would be 0.0 km/h with a death risk of 0.0%.

In the gaps analysis, 78.8% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed. There were 12 gaps of 6 s or more, 7 of them 12 s or more, longest 88.5 s. The first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video. This one is 3.1 minutes with 8 pedestrian crossings and 6 moving vehicles, so rates from it must be treated with caution.

We request that the authority install a raised zebra crossing with a speed table at this location to reduce speeds and provide protected time to cross. We enclose the measurements above and are happy to share the video for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safety improvement at School Lane crossing

We write regarding pedestrian safety outside our school at School Lane crossing. Crossing Watch video measurements over 37.0 minutes (2220.0 s) recorded 40 crossings and 20 vehicles, with an 85th percentile speed of 45.7 km/h.

In that period, 4 of 40 crossings (1 in 10) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3.0 s of the person, including 2 of 40 (1 in 20) within 1.5 s. Exact 95% ranges if this recording is typical are 2.8-23.7% and 0.6-16.9% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson), and 1.1-10.2 and 0.2-7.2 people in a recording this long (Poisson).

PV² was calculated as 0.0 x 10^8 from 65 pedestrians and 32 moving vehicles an hour scaled from 37 minutes of video, with the caveat that a formal check counts the full peak hour and broken tracks can count 1.3x the true count in the drone test.

75.3% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 9 gaps, 7 of them 12 s or more, longest 47.9 s, with the caveat that the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

The most serious near-miss involved a car at 48.1 km/h with a gap of 1.0 s to a person, with an adult death risk of 7.1% if hit by a car front at that speed per Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+. A child hit at 48.1 km/h here would face a 7.1% chance of dying.

A 2nd serious near-miss involved a bus at 23.1 km/h with a gap of 1.4 s to a person, with an adult death risk of 0.8% if hit by a car front at that speed per Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+.

A close pass involved a car at 42.4 km/h with a gap of 1.9 s to a person, with an adult death risk of 1.6% if hit by a car front at that speed per Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+.

A 2nd close pass involved an auto-rickshaw at 26.5 km/h with a gap of 2.7 s to a person.

We request you install a raised zebra crossing with speed table at this location to reduce vehicle speeds and provide protected priority for pedestrians.

We are willing to share the full video and Crossing Watch measurements for your review. Please advise on next steps for assessment.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safety improvement at the Park Avenue crossing

Dear Sir/Madam,

Our school asked for a video review of the Park Avenue crossing. In 17.7 minutes of video, 1062.0 s in total, 5 crossings and 6 vehicles were recorded. 4 of 5 crossings had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person and 2 of 5 within 1.5 s. The 85th percentile speed was 49.8 km/h. 2 crossings had the person arrive first and 2 had the vehicle arrive first.

The review found 2 serious near-misses and 2 close passes. Serious is defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart. Close pass is 1.5 to 3.0 s.

The most serious near-miss had a PET of 0.4 s with an auto-rickshaw at 49.9 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 8.3 percent, compared with 0.6 percent at 20.0 km/h, per Rosén & Sander 2009 for adults 15+ hit by car fronts.

A second serious near-miss had a PET of 1.2 s with a motorcycle at 29.9 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 1.5 percent, compared with 0.3 percent at 10.3 km/h, per the same source.

One close pass had a PET of 2.2 s with a van at 34.3 km/h.

Another close pass had a PET of 2.8 s with a motorcycle at 26.7 km/h.

In that period 90.4 percent of time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, from 4 gaps with 2 of them 12 s or more and longest 22.9 s, with the caveat that the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

The calculated PV² was 0.0 x 10^8 from 17 pedestrians and 20 vehicles an hour scaled from 17.7 minutes of video, with the caveat that a formal check counts the full peak hour and broken tracks can overcount.

We request that you provide a raised zebra crossing with a speed table and a 20 km/h zone with signs and markings at this location.

We are willing to share the video and the measurements with your engineers and to meet on site.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal
Approved by the Head of School

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safety improvement at the Quarry Road crossing

We write as the school using the Quarry Road crossing. A video survey (Crossing Watch, SAM tracking, road-plane geometry, post-encroachment time) measured the following.

Over 8.4 minutes (504.0 s) we counted 3 pedestrian crossings and 20 moving vehicles. The 85th percentile speed was 64.0 km/h. Drivers here routinely ignore the posted 30 km/h speed limit.

3 of 3 crossings (1 in 1) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person; 3 of 3 (1 in 1) within 1.5 s. Exact 95% ranges, if this recording is typical: 29.2-100.0% and 29.2-100.0% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson); 0.6-8.8 and 0.6-8.8 people in a recording this long (Poisson).

We recorded 3 serious near-misses and 0 close passes, where serious means pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart and a close pass is 1.5-3.0 s.

Details of the worst cases:
The most serious near-miss was serious with a PET of 0.2 s involving an auto-rickshaw at 58.4 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front, death risk at 58.4 km/h is 16.2% compared with 0.6% at an impact of 20.0 km/h (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts).
A second serious near-miss had a PET of 0.5 s involving a car at 50.6 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front, death risk at 50.6 km/h is 8.7% compared with 0.6% at an impact of 20.0 km/h.
A third serious near-miss had a PET of 1.1 s involving an auto-rickshaw at 20.0 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front, death risk at 20.0 km/h is 0.6% compared with 0.6% at an impact of 20.0 km/h.

On gaps and engineering context, with their main caveats: PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video; this one is 8.4. Counted: 3 pedestrian crossings, 20 moving vehicles. 56.0% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed: 6 gaps, 5 of them 12 s or more, longest 35.8 s (the first and last are cut short by the video).

We request installation of a raised zebra crossing with speed table and 20 km/h approach signs at this location to lower vehicle speeds toward 20.0 km/h and protect pedestrians.

We are willing to share the video and measurement files for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safety improvement at North Avenue crossing

We write to request a raised zebra crossing at the North Avenue crossing used by our school.

A Crossing Watch video recorded 7.6 minutes (456.0 s) at the site and counted 9 pedestrian crossings and 12 moving vehicles, with an 85th percentile speed of 59.7 km/h.

In that recording 4 of 9 crossings (1 in 2.2) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person and 2 of 9 (1 in 4.5) within 1.5 s. If this recording is typical, exact 95% ranges are 13.7-78.8% and 2.8-60.0% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson) and 1.1-10.2 and 0.2-7.2 people in a recording this long (Poisson).

Of the 4 events within 3 s, 2 were serious (less than 1.5 s apart) and 2 were close passes (1.5-3.0 s).

One serious event had a car at 51.1 km/h with 0.3 s between pedestrian and vehicle on the same spot.
That speed carries an adult death risk of 9.1% if hit by a car front (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+), compared with 0.6% at an impact speed of 20.0 km/h.
A second serious event had a van at 27.7 km/h with 1.3 s between pedestrian and vehicle.
That speed carries an adult death risk of 1.2% if hit, compared with 0.2% at 10.0 km/h.
One close pass had a bus at 57.0 km/h with 2.2 s between pedestrian and vehicle.
That speed carries an adult death risk of 2.3% if hit.
A second close pass had a car at 19.7 km/h with 1.8 s between pedestrian and vehicle.
That speed carries an adult death risk of 0.2% if hit, compared with 0.2% at 9.5 km/h.
The time gaps are post-encroachment times from SAM tracking and road-plane geometry, and the individual road user was not reviewed.

The video also showed 43.5% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, from 10 gaps with 4 of them 12 s or more and the longest 82.5 s.
We note the first and last gaps are cut short by the video, and that PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video while this recording is 7.6 minutes with 9 crossings and 12 vehicles, so those rates should be treated with caution.

We request installation of a raised zebra crossing at this location to slow traffic and establish priority for pedestrians.

We are willing to share the video and underlying measurements on request.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

We write on behalf of the school regarding the pedestrian crossing outside our premises. We commissioned a 10.9 minute video recording (654.0 s) analysed with SAM tracking and road-plane geometry. In that time there were 7 pedestrian crossings and 6 moving vehicles.

The second serious near-miss involved an auto-rickshaw with a post-encroachment time of 0.2 s. The auto-rickshaw speed was 42.2 km/h. The third serious near-miss involved a car with a post-encroachment time of 1.1 s. The car speed was 24.6 km/h.

Yours faithfully,

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safer crossing outside the school on Lake View Road

We write regarding the crossing outside our school on Lake View Road. A Crossing Watch review of 21.4 minutes of video (1284.0 s) recorded 11 crossings and 22 vehicles, with an 85th percentile speed of 50.9 km/h. To sum up, the recording showed 3 serious near-misses and 1 close pass.

The review found 4 of 11 crossings (1 in 2.8) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person, and 3 of 11 (1 in 3.7) within 1.5 s. Exact 95% ranges, if this recording is typical, are 10.9-69.2% and 6.0-61.0% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson) and 1.1-10.2 and 0.6-8.8 people in a recording this long (Poisson). There were 3 serious near-misses and 1 close pass as defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart and 1.5-3.0 s respectively.

The worst near-misses were:
One serious near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 0.1 s with a car at 51.3 km/h. The adult death risk if hit by a car front at that speed is 9.2% from Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts, compared to 0.6% at an impact of 20.0 km/h under a 20 km/h limit.
Another serious near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 0.7 s with an auto-rickshaw at 42.7 km/h. The adult death risk if hit by a car front at that speed is 4.5%, compared to 0.6% at an impact of 20.0 km/h.
Another serious near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 0.3 s with an auto-rickshaw at 37.7 km/h. The adult death risk if hit by a car front at that speed is 2.9%, compared to 0.6% at an impact of 20.0 km/h.
One close pass had a post-encroachment time of 1.7 s with a car at 51.5 km/h. The adult death risk if hit by a car front at that speed is 6.1%.

In engineering terms, PV² was 0.0 x 10^8 from 31 pedestrians and 62 moving vehicles an hour, scaled from 21.4 minutes of video, and a formal check counts the full peak hour and broken tracks can count one twice as 1.3x the true count in our drone test. Also 43.6% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 3 gaps and 1 of them 12 s or more and longest 17.6 s, with the caveat that the first and last are cut short by the video.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing with a speed table at this location to reduce vehicle speeds and provide a protected crossing.

We are willing to share the video and the Crossing Watch measurements for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

Dear Sir/Madam,

Re: Safety at Garden Road crossing

We write to request a raised zebra crossing outside our school. Crossing Watch video measurements (SAM tracking, road-plane geometry, post-encroachment time) recorded 33 crossings and 7 vehicles in 32.9 minutes (1974.0 s).

The 85th percentile speed was 51.9 km/h. Over half of drivers were exceeding the posted speed limit. There were 0 serious near-misses and 3 close passes. By definition a serious near-miss is pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart and a close pass is 1.5 s to 3.0 s apart. Of the 3 close passes, the pedestrian was first in 2 and the vehicle was first in 1.

The closest was 1.5 s involving a car at 41.9 km/h with an adult death risk of 4.2% if hit by a car front (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+).
A second close pass was 1.7 s involving an auto-rickshaw at 46.4 km/h with an adult death risk of 3.9% if hit.
A third close pass was 1.9 s involving a van at 28.9 km/h with an adult death risk of 0.4% if hit.

For context, PV² was 0.0 x 10^8 based on 60 pedestrians and 13 moving vehicles per hour scaled from 32.9 minutes of video; a formal check counts the full peak hour and broken tracks can overcount.
Also 50.7% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 12 gaps of 6 s or more, 12 of them 12 s or more, longest 22.3 s; the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing at this location to lower speeds and give pedestrians priority. We are happy to share the video and measurements for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safety improvement at Orchard Lane crossing

Dear Sir/Madam,

We write as the school beside Orchard Lane crossing. During 17.2 minutes, 10 crossings and 39 vehicles were observed. From video of the crossing we measured 10 crossings and 39 vehicles in 17.2 minutes (1032.0 s), with an 85th percentile speed of 60.5 km/h.

6 of 10 crossings (1 in 1.7) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person. 3 of 10 (1 in 3.3) had a vehicle within 1.5 s. Exact 95% ranges, if this recording is typical, are 26.2-87.8% and 6.7-65.2% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson) and 2.2-13.1 and 0.6-8.8 people in a recording this long (Poisson).

By definition serious is pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart and close pass is 1.5-3.0 s. There were 3 serious near-misses and 3 close passes. Person first was 4, vehicle first was 2 and both at once was 0.

One serious near-miss involved a motorcycle at 53.4 km/h with 0.8 s between pedestrian and vehicle on the same spot. Another serious near-miss involved a van at 44.1 km/h with 0.7 s between pedestrian and vehicle on the same spot. A third serious near-miss involved a car at 14.6 km/h with 0.1 s between pedestrian and vehicle on the same spot.

One close pass involved a bus at 36.1 km/h with 1.7 s between pedestrian and vehicle on the same spot. Another close pass involved an auto-rickshaw at 31.1 km/h with 1.8 s between pedestrian and vehicle on the same spot.

For adults hit by a car front, the modelled death risks for those events would be 11.0% for the motorcycle case, 5.1% for the van case, 0.4% for the car case, 1.6% for the bus case and 0.7% for the auto-rickshaw case (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+).

On engineering context, PV² was 0.0 x 10^8, calculated as 35 pedestrians and 136 moving vehicles an hour scaled from 17.2 minutes of video; a formal check counts the full peak hour and broken tracks can count one person twice, 1.3x the true count in our drone test. 51.9% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 6 gaps, 2 of them 12 s or more and the longest 38.3 s, noting the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request you install a raised zebra crossing with speed table at this crossing to enforce lower speeds at the conflict point and give pedestrians priority.

We are happy to share the video and measurement log for your review and to discuss further.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safety improvement at Orchard Lane crossing

We are writing about the safety of the Orchard Lane crossing outside our school. Crossing Watch measured the crossing with SAM tracking and road-plane geometry for 35.4 minutes (2124.0 s). In that time there were 9 crossings and 10 vehicles. The 85th percentile speed was 46.4 km/h.

Of the 9 crossings, 2 of 9 crossings (1 in 4.5) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person, and 2 of 9 (1 in 4.5) within 1.5 s. Exact 95% ranges, if this recording is typical, are 2.8-60.0% and 2.8-60.0% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson) and 0.2-7.2 and 0.2-7.2 people in a recording this long (Poisson).

There were 2 serious near-misses, defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart. The 2124.0 s observation counted 9 crossings plus 10 vehicles alongside 0 close passes. The most serious involved a bus at 39.2 km/h with a post-encroachment time of 0.3 s. At 39.2 km/h the death risk if an adult is hit by a car front is 3.3% (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts), compared with 0.6% at an impact of 20.0 km/h at a 20 km/h limit.

The other serious near-miss involved a car at 32.0 km/h with a post-encroachment time of 0.7 s. At 32.0 km/h the death risk if an adult is hit by a car front is 1.8%, compared with 0.6% at an impact of 20.0 km/h at a 20 km/h limit.

For context, PV² was 0.0 x 10^8 (15 pedestrians and 17 moving vehicles an hour), scaled from 35.4 minutes of video; a formal check counts the full peak hour and broken tracks can count one twice. 91.5% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed (4 gaps, longest 10.7 s; the first and last are cut short by the video).

We request that you provide a raised zebra crossing with speed table at this location to reduce speeds and give pedestrians priority. We have the video and measurement data and are happy to share them for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for a safer crossing outside the school

We measured activity at the crossing outside the school for 40.6 minutes (2436.0 s). In that time we recorded 22 crossings and 29 moving vehicles, with an 85th percentile speed of 41.9 km/h. Near-misses like these occur every morning when school opens.

Of the 22 crossings, 4 (1 in 5.5) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3.0 s of the person, and 1 of 22 (1 in 22) was within 1.5 s. We class serious as less than 1.5 s apart and close pass as 1.5-3.0 s. There was 1 serious near-miss and 3 close passes.

The most serious was a car at 40.2 km/h passing 1.0 s after the person. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 3.6% (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts).

A second event was a motorcycle at 31.3 km/h with a gap of 2.5 s.

A third event was a van at 42.5 km/h with a gap of 2.5 s.

A fourth event was a car at 23.0 km/h with a gap of 2.9 s.

For context, PV² was 0.0 x 10^8 when scaled as 33 pedestrians and 43 moving vehicles an hour from 40.6 minutes of video, noting a formal check counts the full peak hour. 67.7% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more, with 4 such gaps including 1 of 12 s or more and a longest gap of 60.8 s, noting the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing with speed table at this location.

We can share the video and tracking data on request.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for a safer crossing outside the school on Park Avenue

Dear Sir/Madam,

Our school monitored the crossing outside it for 38.4 minutes (2304.0 s). In that time we recorded 32 crossings and 17 vehicles. The 85th percentile speed was 26.3 km/h. The people crossing in these events were our students. We observed 1 serious near-miss and 2 close passes.

By definition, a serious near-miss is when a pedestrian and a moving vehicle are on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart, and a close pass is 1.5 to 3.0 s apart.

The serious near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 1.4 s and involved a car at 14.2 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at 14.2 km/h the death risk from Rosén & Sander 2009 is 0.4%.

A close pass had a post-encroachment time of 2.1 s and involved a van at 13.8 km/h.

A further close pass had a post-encroachment time of 2.4 s and involved a car at 24.6 km/h.

For context, PV² was 0.0 x 10^8 based on 50 pedestrians and 27 moving vehicles an hour scaled from 38.4 minutes of video, with the caveat that a formal check counts the full peak hour and that broken tracks can count one person twice, by 1.3x in our drone test. 

Also, 67.0% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 8 gaps and 7 of them 12 s or more and longest gap 33.8 s, with the caveat that the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request you provide a raised zebra crossing with a speed table at this crossing to reduce vehicle speeds and to give pedestrians priority.

We are happy to share the video and Crossing Watch measurements to assist your assessment.

Yours faithfully,

The Principal

Yours faithfully,

The Principal

Subject: Request for safety improvements at Market Street crossing

We write to request a raised zebra crossing with speed table at Market Street crossing.

Crossing Watch measured the crossing for 25.5 minutes and recorded 35 crossings and 21 vehicles. The 85th percentile speed was 58.3 km/h. Several drivers were looking at mobile phones as they passed through the crossing. 5 of 35 crossings (1 in 7) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person. 5 of 35 (1 in 7) were within 1.5 s, defined as serious where pedestrian and moving vehicle are on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart. On this basis the exact 95% ranges, if this recording is typical, are 4.8-30.3% of crossings and 1.6-11.7 people in a recording this long.

The most severe serious near-miss had a time gap of 0.7 s with an auto-rickshaw at 56.5 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the modelled death risk is 14.0% (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts).
Another serious near-miss had a time gap of 0.9 s with a van at 54.1 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the modelled death risk is 11.6%.
Another serious near-miss had a time gap of 1.2 s with a motorcycle at 24.5 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the modelled death risk is 0.9%.
Another serious near-miss had a time gap of 0.8 s with a motorcycle at 20.1 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the modelled death risk is 0.6%.
Another serious near-miss had a time gap of 0.9 s with a car at 15.3 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the modelled death risk is 0.4%.

For engineering context, PV² was calculated as 0.0 x 10^8, scaled from 25.5 minutes of video, and 67.5% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 2 gaps of 6 s or more and a longest gap of 11.6 s, noting the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing with speed table to reduce vehicle speeds and provide a protected crossing point. We are willing to share the video and measurements for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

Dear Sir/Madam,

We write about safety at the River Lane crossing. Crossing Watch measurements (SAM tracking, road-plane geometry, post-encroachment time) recorded 19.2 minutes (1152.0 s) with 15 crossings and 24 vehicles.

During that period 5 of 15 crossings (1 in 3) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person, and 3 of 15 (1 in 5) within 1.5 s. Exact 95% ranges, if this recording is typical, are 11.8-61.6% and 4.3-48.1% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson), and 1.6-11.7 and 0.6-8.8 people in a recording this long (Poisson). The 85th percentile speed was 52.5 km/h.

The worst serious near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 0.8 s with a motorcycle at 49.9 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 8.2% (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts).

A second serious near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 1.1 s with a motorcycle at 22.4 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 0.8%.

A third serious near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 1.4 s with a van at 14.9 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 0.4%.

A close pass had a post-encroachment time of 1.5 s with a van at 40.2 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 3.6%.

A further close pass had a post-encroachment time of 1.9 s with a car at 47.0 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 2.4%.

For context, PV² was 0.0 x 10^8 (47 pedestrians and 75 moving vehicles an hour scaled from 19.2 minutes of video; a formal check counts the full peak hour). 64.2% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 11 such gaps and 4 of 12 s or more and the longest 27.1 s (the first and last gaps are cut short by the video).

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing with a speed table at this location to reduce vehicle speeds and provide protected priority for pedestrians.

We have the video and tracking data and are happy to share them for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority,

We write concerning the Station Road crossing outside our school. In 26.9 minutes (1614.0 s) of video we recorded 33 crossings and 3 moving vehicles. The 1614.0 s sample contained 33 crossings alongside 3 vehicles.

The 85th percentile speed was 54.3 km/h.

We observed 2 serious near-misses, defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart, and 1 close pass defined as 1.5-3.0 s apart.

Of the 3 events, in 0 the person was first, in 2 the vehicle was first, and in 1 both were at once.

The most serious event had a post-encroachment time of 0.0 s with a car travelling at 47.3 km/h, carrying an adult death risk of 6.6% if hit (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts), which would fall to 0.6% at an impact speed of 20.0 km/h.

A second serious event had a post-encroachment time of 0.1 s with a car travelling at 36.1 km/h, carrying an adult death risk of 2.5% if hit, which would also fall to 0.6% at an impact speed of 20.0 km/h.

A close pass event had a post-encroachment time of 2.7 s with a van travelling at 37.3 km/h.

For engineering context, PV² was 0.0 x 10^8 based on 74 pedestrians and 7 moving vehicles an hour scaled from 26.9 minutes of video, while a formal check counts the full peak hour. 60.4% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, from 4 gaps with longest 8.4 s, noting the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing with a 20 km/h zone and signs at this location.

We are willing to share the full video and Crossing Watch data for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

Dear Sir/Madam,

I write on behalf of the school regarding the Mill Street crossing. Many pupils cross here alone each morning without adult supervision.

We commissioned a video measurement of 7.8 minutes (468.0 s) covering 3 pedestrian crossings and 6 moving vehicles. The 85th percentile speed was 20.3 km/h. PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video; this one is 7.8. Counted: 3 pedestrian crossings, 6 moving vehicles. The first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

During this period there was 1 serious near-miss, defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart. In the worst case the vehicle was a car travelling at 19.5 km/h. The post-encroachment time was 0.3 s. For an adult hit by a car front at 19.5 km/h the estimated death risk is 0.6% (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts). At a 20 km/h limit the estimated impact speed would be 19.5 km/h with a death risk of 0.6% for an adult. The road user involved was not reviewed.

UK Traffic Signs Manual ch. 6 (13.5.2) notes that 4 to 6 s is an acceptable gap at urban speeds; other groups, such as children, may need 10 to 12 s or longer.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing at this location to provide a protected crossing and reduce vehicle speeds.

We are willing to share the video and the full measurement report.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
Dear Sir/Madam,

We write concerning Orchard Lane crossing. In 28.8 minutes (1728.0 s) of video we recorded 24 crossings and 17 vehicles. The 85th percentile speed was 38.8 mph. Of the 24 crossings, 4 of 24 (1 in 6) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s and 3 of 24 (1 in 8) within 1.5 s.

The recording showed 3 serious near-misses defined as less than 1.5 s apart and 1 close pass defined as 1.5-3.0 s. One serious near-miss involved an auto-rickshaw at 32.1 km/h with a PET of 0.7 s. The adult death risk if hit by a car front at that speed is 1.8% (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+).

A second serious near-miss involved a bus at 31.6 km/h with a PET of 0.9 s. The adult death risk if hit by a car front at that speed is 1.7%.

A third serious near-miss involved an auto-rickshaw at 19.7 km/h with a PET of 1.4 s. The adult death risk if hit by a car front at that speed is 0.6%.

The close pass involved a car at 17.0 km/h with a PET of 1.8 s. The adult death risk if hit by a car front at that speed is 0.2%.

For context, PV² was 0.0 x 10^8 scaled from 28.8 minutes of video, while a formal check counts the full peak hour. 45.4% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 9 gaps and longest 76.0 s, but the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request a raised zebra crossing with speed table at this location to lower vehicle speeds and protect people crossing. We are happy to share the video and measurements for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safety improvement at Station Road crossing

Dear Sir/Madam,

We measured road use outside our school at Station Road crossing for 37.0 minutes (2220.0 s). In that time we recorded 21 crossings and 8 vehicles. The 85th percentile speed was 49.0 km/h.

Of the 21 crossings, 4 of 21 (1 in 5.2) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person, and 4 of 21 (1 in 5.2) within 1.5 s. The exact 95% ranges if this recording is typical are 5.4-41.9% and 5.4-41.9% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson), and 1.1-10.2 and 1.1-10.2 people in a recording this long (Poisson). There were 4 serious near-misses (pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart) and 0 close passes (1.5-3.0 s). Of these, 2 were person first and 2 were vehicle first.

The 4 worst serious near-misses were as follows. A bus at 49.3 km/h was 1.0 s apart from a person. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 7.8% (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts). A van at 18.9 km/h was 0.4 s apart from a person. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 0.6%. An auto-rickshaw at 17.2 km/h was 1.4 s apart from a person. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 0.5%. A van at 14.2 km/h was 0.2 s apart from a person. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 0.4%.

For context, the engineering review noted PV² = 0.0 x 10^8, based on 34 pedestrians and 13 moving vehicles an hour scaled from 37 minutes of video, with the caveat that a formal check counts the full peak hour. It also noted 41.5% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, from 1 gap including 1 of 12 s or more and a longest gap of 55.2 s, with the caveat that the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request you install a raised zebra crossing with speed table at Station Road crossing to reduce vehicle speeds and provide a protected crossing point.

We have the video and tracking data and are happy to share them for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal
