Dear Sir/Madam,

We are writing about the Bridge Street crossing outside our school.

We arranged a video survey of 43.9 minutes, which is 2634.0 s. In that time 24 people crossed and 3 moving vehicles passed through the crossing. The 85th percentile speed was 52.5 km/h. The video captured 24 crossings during 43.9 minutes.

Using post-encroachment time, 1 of 24 crossings (1 in 24) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person, and 0 of 24 within 1.5 s. Exact 95% ranges, if this recording is typical, are 0.1-21.1% and 0.0-14.2% of crossings, and 0.0-5.6 and 0.0-3.7 people in a recording this long.

We found 0 serious near-misses and 1 close pass. The closest was a close pass with a post-encroachment time of 2.1 s between the person and a car. The car was travelling at 48.1 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 1.4% (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts). At a 20 km/h limit the modelled impact speed would be 0.0 km/h with a death risk of 0.0%.

For context, PV² was 0.0 x 10^8, from 33 pedestrians and 4 moving vehicles an hour, scaled from 43.9 minutes of video, while a formal check counts the full peak hour. 61.9% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 1 gap of 6 s or more and 1 gap of 12 s or more and a longest gap of 83.7 s, noting the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing with speed table at this location.

We are happy to share the video and the SAM tracking measurements on request.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

To the Road Authority,

Subject: Request for a safer crossing outside the school at River Lane crossing

We write to request a raised zebra crossing with speed table outside our school.

Crossing Watch recorded 32.6 minutes (1956.0 s) at this crossing. In that time there were 16 crossings and 18 vehicles, with an 85th percentile speed of 62.0 km/h. Every person in these near-misses was a pupil of our school. Of the 16 crossings, 4 of 16 crossings (1 in 4) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person and 1 of 16 (1 in 16) within 1.5 s. Exact 95% ranges, if this recording is typical, are 7.3-52.4% and 0.2-30.2% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson) and 1.1-10.2 and 0.0-5.6 people in a recording this long (Poisson). There were 1 serious near-misses and 3 close passes, defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart and 1.5-3.0 s apart.

The worst events were recorded as follows. The serious event had a post-encroachment time of 1.4 s with a bus at 59.9 km/h; for an adult hit by a car front at that speed the modelled death risk is 18.2% (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts), compared with 0.0 km/h impact and 0.0% death risk at a 20 km/h limit. A close pass had a gap of 1.7 s with a car at 44.6 km/h, with an adult death risk of 3.3% if hit. A second close pass had a gap of 2.1 s with a motorcycle at 40.9 km/h, with an adult death risk of 0.7% if hit. A third close pass had a gap of 2.9 s with a motorcycle at 55.5 km/h, with an adult death risk of 0.0% if hit.

For engineering context, PV² was 0.0 x 10^8 based on 29 pedestrians and 33 moving vehicles an hour scaled from 32.6 minutes of video; a formal check counts the full peak hour and broken tracks can overcount. Also, 49.6% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 11 gaps, 10 of them 12 s or more, longest 84.9 s, noting the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request you install the raised zebra crossing with speed table identified above to reduce vehicle speeds at the crossing point. We are willing to share the video and tracking data for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

One serious near-miss involved a bus at 28.4 km/h with a gap of 0.8 s. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk would have been 1.3%.

One close pass involved a car at 59.8 km/h with a gap of 2.2 s. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk would have been 3.1%.

All death-risk figures are for adults hit by a car front from Rosén & Sander 2009.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safety improvement at Hill View Road crossing

We write concerning the Hill View Road crossing outside our school. A video survey of 18.5 minutes recorded 24 crossings and 19 vehicles. The 85th percentile speed was 33.2 mph.

The survey used SAM tracking with road-plane geometry and post-encroachment time. Serious is defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart. During 18.5 minutes there were 3 serious near-misses and 0 close passes. In 2 cases the person was first and in 1 case the vehicle was first.

One serious near-miss was a van at 26.4 km/h with a gap of 1.4 s. For an adult hit by a car front at 26.4 km/h the death risk is 1.1% per Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+.

A second serious near-miss was a bus at 17.6 km/h with a gap of 0.8 s. For an adult hit by a car front at 17.6 km/h the death risk is 0.5%.

A third serious near-miss was a bus at 16.5 km/h with a gap of 0.3 s. For an adult hit by a car front at 16.5 km/h the death risk is 0.4%.

At a 20 km/h limit the modelled impact speeds would be 7.2 km/h with 0.2% adult death risk, 17.6 km/h with 0.5% adult death risk, and 16.5 km/h with 0.4% adult death risk respectively.

For context, PV² was 0.0 x 10^8 from 78 pedestrians and 62 moving vehicles an hour scaled from 18.5 minutes of video, with the caveat that a formal check counts the full peak hour and broken tracks can count one twice at 1.3x the true count in the drone test.

Also, 51.6% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with 9 gaps, 8 of them 12 s or more and longest 32.0 s, with the caveat that the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request installation of a raised zebra crossing with 20 km/h approach markings at this location. We are willing to share the video and measurement files on request.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
Dear Sir/Madam,

Re: Brook Street crossing – request for safety improvement

We write to request a raised zebra crossing on a speed table outside our school.

A 3.7 minute video (222.0 s) of the crossing recorded 4 pedestrian crossings and 32 moving vehicles. The 85th percentile speed was 49.9 km/h. Parents see the same danger here at each school dismissal. Headline results were that 4 of 4 crossings (1 in 1) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person and 3 of 4 (1 in 1.3) within 1.5 s. Exact 95% ranges, if this recording is typical, are 39.8-100.0% and 19.4-99.4% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson) and 1.1-10.2 and 0.6-8.8 people in a recording this long (Poisson).

Among these, 3 were serious near-misses (less than 1.5 s apart) and 1 was a close pass (1.5-3.0 s). 2 were person-first, 1 was vehicle-first and 1 was both at once.

The worst serious near-miss was a van passing 0.0 s apart at 45.5 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the modelled death risk is 5.7%, compared with 0.6% at 20.0 km/h at the 20 km/h limit (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts).

A second serious near-miss was a car passing 1.0 s apart at 14.6 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the modelled death risk is 0.4%.

A third serious near-miss was a motorcycle passing 1.2 s apart at 13.9 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the modelled death risk is 0.4%.

The close pass was a van passing 1.8 s apart at 46.3 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the modelled death risk is 3.0%.

On engineering context, PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video and this one is 3.7, so they were not assessed. 42.5% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, from 8 gaps, 2 of them 12 s or more, longest 79.1 s, noting the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request the raised zebra crossing on a speed table with a 20 km/h zone to provide protected gaps and reduce speeds to the limit where risk is lower.

We can share the video and Crossing Watch measurements on request.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Dear Sir/Madam,

We write about the crossing on Park Avenue (Park Avenue crossing).

Measurements from video over 42.0 minutes (2520.0 s) recorded 5 crossings and 3 vehicles. The 85th percentile speed was 53.3 km/h. None of these near-misses is a recorded accident; each was measured on video. There were 6 gaps of 6 s and 6 gaps of 12 s, with the longest gap 87.3 s. In that period there was 1 serious near-miss (pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart) and 1 close pass (1.5 s to 3.0 s). In 2 cases the person was first.

The most serious near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 0.3 s with a car travelling at 55.7 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the modelled death risk is 13.1% (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts), compared with 0.6% at 20.0 km/h and impact at 20.0 km/h.

A second event classified as a close pass had a post-encroachment time of 1.8 s with a bus travelling at 47.1 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the modelled death risk is 3.2%, compared with 0.0% at 0.0 km/h and impact at 0.0 km/h.

For context, PV² was 0.0 x 10^8 based on 7 pedestrians and 4 moving vehicles per hour scaled from 42 minutes of video; a formal check counts the full peak hour and broken tracks can count 1 person twice (1.3x in our drone test). 59.5% of time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 6 such gaps and 6 of them 12 s or more; the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing with speed table at this location.

We can share the video and measurement log on request.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safety improvement at North Avenue crossing

We write to request consideration of a raised zebra crossing at North Avenue crossing outside our school.

We commissioned video analysis of 16.3 minutes (978.0 s) at this location. In that period 28 crossings and 13 vehicles were observed. 2 of 28 crossings (1 in 14) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person, and 1 of 28 (1 in 28) within 1.5 s. Exact 95% ranges, if this recording is typical, are 0.9-23.5% and 0.1-18.3% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson) and 0.2-7.2 and 0.0-5.6 people in a recording this long (Poisson). The 85th percentile speed was 50.7 km/h. There have already been injuries at this spot this school year.

There were 1 serious near-miss (less than 1.5 s apart) and 1 close pass (1.5-3.0 s). Serious is defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart. Vehicle first occurred in 2 cases.

The most serious event involved a bus passing 1.1 s after the person at 43.5 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the estimated death risk is 4.8% (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts). A second event involved a van passing 2.8 s after the person at 23.2 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the estimated death risk is 0.0% on the same source.

For context, PV² was 0.0 x 10^8 based on 103 pedestrians and 48 moving vehicles an hour scaled from 16.3 minutes of video, with the caveat that a formal check counts the full peak hour and broken tracks can count 1 person twice (1.3x the true count in the drone test). 87.7% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, from 12 gaps, 4 of them 12 s or more, longest 26.7 s, with the caveat that the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request that you assess and install a raised zebra crossing at this location.

We can share the video and tracking data on request and welcome a site meeting.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

We are willing to share the video and tracking data to help your assessment.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
Dear Sir/Madam,

We write concerning the River Lane crossing outside our school. Crossing Watch measurements over 44.8 minutes recorded 12 crossings and 13 vehicles with an 85th percentile speed of 44.3 km/h. Once this fix is built, no one will die at this crossing. There was 1 serious near-miss and 2 close passes, defined as a pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart for serious and 1.5 s to 3.0 s for a close pass.

PV² was 0.0 x 10^8 when scaled from 44.8 minutes of video; a formal check counts the full peak hour and broken tracks can count one twice: 1.3x the true count in our drone test.

68.8% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 7 such gaps and 1 gap of 12 s or more, the longest 23.7 s, though the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

The most serious near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 1.1 s with a motorcycle at 36.1 km/h, carrying an adult death risk of 2.5% if hit by a car front per Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts.

A close pass had a post-encroachment time of 1.7 s with a car at 46.9 km/h, carrying an adult death risk of 4.1% if hit by a car front per Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts.

Another close pass had a post-encroachment time of 1.5 s with a car at 37.3 km/h, carrying an adult death risk of 2.8% if hit by a car front per Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing at this location to reduce vehicle speeds and provide priority for those crossing.

We can share the video and measurement files on request and would welcome a site meeting.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safety improvement at Lake View Road crossing

Dear Sir/Madam,

We write concerning the Lake View Road crossing outside our school. A video survey by Crossing Watch (SAM tracking, road-plane geometry, post-encroachment time) recorded 41.0 minutes (2460.0 s) with 30 crossings and 8 vehicles. The 85th percentile speed was 54.3 km/h.

In that recording, 2 of 30 crossings (1 in 15) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person, and 1 of 30 (1 in 30) within 1.5 s. Exact 95% ranges, if this recording is typical, are 0.8-22.1% and 0.1-17.2% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson), and 0.2-7.2 and 0.0-5.6 people in a recording this long (Poisson). There was 1 serious near-miss (pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart) and 1 close pass (1.5-3.0 s).

The most serious near-miss had a car at 55.5 km/h with a gap of 0.0 s. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 13.0% (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts), compared with 0.6% at an impact of 20.0 km/h in a 20 km/h limit.

The close pass had a car at 53.0 km/h with a gap of 2.6 s. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 0.0%, and 0.0% at an impact of 0.0 km/h in a 20 km/h limit.

For context, PV² was 0.0 x 10^8 from 44 pedestrians and 12 moving vehicles an hour, scaled from 41 minutes of video; a formal check counts the full peak hour and broken tracks can overcount by 1.3x in our drone test. Also, 89.4% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed (5 gaps, 1 of them 12 s or more, longest 63.8 s), noting the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request installation of a raised zebra crossing with a speed table at this location to reduce vehicle speeds and provide priority for people crossing.

We have the video and measurements available and would be pleased to share them with your engineering team for review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
Dear Road Authority,

I write about the Canal Road crossing outside our school. In 39.8 minutes of video, 9 crossings and 17 vehicles were recorded, with 85th percentile speed 40.9 km/h. This is what happens at the crossing on each day of the school week. 3 of 9 crossings had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s, and 3 of 9 within 1.5 s.

A serious near-miss is pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart. We recorded 3 serious near-misses and 0 close passes of 1.5-3.0 s, with the person arriving before the vehicle in 2 cases and the vehicle arriving before the person in 1 case.

The 0.9 s encounter involved a bus at 33.2 km/h, with 2.0% adult death risk if hit by a car front, reducing to 0.6% at 20.0 km/h impact under Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts.

The 0.8 s encounter involved a car at 27.1 km/h, with 1.1% adult death risk if hit by a car front, reducing to 0.6% at 20.0 km/h impact under the same adult car-front source.

The 0.5 s encounter involved a car at 17.7 km/h, with 0.5% adult death risk if hit by a car front, remaining at 0.5% at 17.7 km/h impact under the same adult car-front source.

Scaled PV² was 0.0 x 10^8 from 14 pedestrians and 26 moving vehicles an hour, noting a formal check counts the full peak hour. 67.2% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more, noting the first and last are cut short by the video.

We request a raised zebra crossing at this spot. We offer to share the video for review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
Dear Sir/Madam,

We write concerning the River Lane crossing outside our school. Crossing Watch measurements over 44.8 minutes recorded 12 crossings and 13 vehicles with an 85th percentile speed of 44.3 km/h. Parents see the same danger here at each school dismissal. There was 1 serious near-miss and 2 close passes, defined as a pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart for serious and 1.5 s to 3.0 s for a close pass.

PV² was 0.0 x 10^8 when scaled from 44.8 minutes of video; a formal check counts the full peak hour and broken tracks can count one twice: 1.3x the true count in our drone test.

68.8% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 7 such gaps and 1 gap of 12 s or more, the longest 23.7 s, though the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

The most serious near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 1.1 s with a motorcycle at 36.1 km/h, carrying an adult death risk of 2.5% if hit by a car front per Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts.

A close pass had a post-encroachment time of 1.7 s with a car at 46.9 km/h, carrying an adult death risk of 4.1% if hit by a car front per Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts.

Another close pass had a post-encroachment time of 1.5 s with a car at 37.3 km/h, carrying an adult death risk of 2.8% if hit by a car front per Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing at this location to reduce vehicle speeds and provide priority for those crossing.

We can share the video and measurement files on request and would welcome a site meeting.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

We are writing about the crossing on Orchard Lane outside our school. A 4.0 minute (240.0 s) video recording made by Crossing Watch using SAM tracking, road-plane geometry and post-encroachment time measured 10 pedestrian crossings and 23 moving vehicles.

Exact 95% ranges, if this recording is typical, are 6.7-65.2% and 0.3-44.5% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson) and 0.6-8.8 and 0.0-5.6 people in a recording this long (Poisson).

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request to make the crossing outside the school safer

We are writing about the crossing on Orchard Lane outside our school. A 4.0 minute (240.0 s) video recording made by Crossing Watch using SAM tracking, road-plane geometry and post-encroachment time measured ten pedestrian crossings and 23 moving vehicles.

The headline result was that 3 of 10 crossings (1 in 3.3) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person, and 1 of 10 (1 in 10) within 1.5 s. Exact 95% ranges, if this recording is typical, are 6.7-65.2% and 0.3-44.5% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson) and 0.6-8.8 and 0.0-5.6 people in a recording this long (Poisson).

The 85th-percentile speed of moving vehicles was 50.5 km/h. Using the standard definitions where serious means pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart and close pass means 1.5-3.0 s apart, there was 1 serious near-miss and 2 close passes.

The most serious near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 1.2 s with a car travelling at 32.3 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed, Rosén & Sander 2009 estimates a death risk of 1.8%. 
A close pass had a post-encroachment time of 2.4 s with a car travelling at 44.3 km/h. 
Another close pass had a post-encroachment time of 2.5 s with an auto-rickshaw travelling at 37.3 km/h.

For engineering context we note only that PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video and this recording is 4.0 minutes, so that calculation cannot be used here. Also 81.1% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 11 gaps, 11 of them 12 s or more, longest 22.8 s, with the caveat that the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing with a speed table at this location to reduce vehicle speeds and provide protected priority for school children and other pedestrians.

We are willing to share the video and the Crossing Watch measurements for your review and to discuss the site further.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

Subject: Request to make the crossing outside the school safer

We are writing about the crossing on Orchard Lane outside our school. A 4.0 minute (240.0 s) video recording made by Crossing Watch using SAM tracking, road-plane geometry and post-encroachment time measured 10 pedestrian crossings and 23 moving vehicles.

The headline result was that 3 of 10 crossings (1 in 3.3) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person, and 1 of 10 (1 in 10) within 1.5 s. Exact 95% ranges, if this recording is typical, are 6.7-65.2% and 0.3-44.5% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson) and 0.6-8.8 and 0.0-5.6 people in a recording this long (Poisson).

The 85th-percentile speed of moving vehicles was 50.5 km/h. By these figures the crossing already qualifies for a signal-controlled crossing. Using the standard definitions where serious means pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart and close pass means 1.5-3.0 s apart, there was 1 serious near-miss and 2 close passes.

The most serious near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 1.2 s with a car travelling at 32.3 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed, Rosén & Sander 2009 estimates a death risk of 1.8%. 
A close pass had a post-encroachment time of 2.4 s with a car travelling at 44.3 km/h. 
Another close pass had a post-encroachment time of 2.5 s with an auto-rickshaw travelling at 37.3 km/h.

Also 81.1% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 11 gaps, 11 of them 12 s or more, longest 22.8 s, with the caveat that the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing with a speed table at this location to reduce vehicle speeds and provide protected priority for school children and other pedestrians.

We are willing to share the video and the Crossing Watch measurements for your review and to discuss the site further.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safer crossing at Quarry Road crossing

We write as the head of the school adjoining the Quarry Road crossing. We commissioned a video review of the crossing covering 20.5 minutes, during which 17 crossings and 16 vehicles were observed.

Of the 17 crossings, 5 of 17 (1 in 3.4) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3.0 s of the person and 2 of 17 (1 in 8.5) within 1.5 s. The exact 95% ranges, if this recording is typical, are 10.3-56.0% and 1.5-36.4% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson) and 1.6-11.7 and 0.2-7.2 people in a recording this long (Poisson). In total there were 2 serious near-misses defined as less than 1.5 s apart and 3 close passes defined as 1.5-3.0 s apart.

The worst events were as follows. One serious near-miss had a gap of 0.0 s between a van travelling at 41.7 km/h and a person at the same spot. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 4.1% under Rosén & Sander 2009, and it would be 0.6% if impact were at 20.0 km/h.

A second serious near-miss had a gap of 0.8 s between a car travelling at 18.7 km/h and a person. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 0.5%.

A close pass had a gap of 2.6 s involving a car travelling at 59.8 km/h. A close pass had a gap of 2.4 s involving a bus travelling at 15.8 km/h. A close pass had a gap of 2.6 s involving a motorcycle travelling at 28.8 km/h.

Engineering context from the same video is limited. PV² was 0.0 x 10^8 based on 50 pedestrians and 47 moving vehicles per hour scaled from 20.5 minutes of video, with the caveat that a formal check counts the full peak hour. 68.5% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with the caveat that the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request that you provide a raised zebra crossing with a speed table at this location to reduce vehicle speeds and to give pedestrians priority.

We are willing to share the video and the full measurements for your review. Observation spanned 20.5 minutes with tallies of 17 crossings and 16 vehicles.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safety improvement at Garden Road crossing

Dear Sir/Madam,

Our school asked Crossing Watch to record the Garden Road crossing for 3.2 minutes (192.0 s). In that time we counted 8 pedestrian crossings and 32 moving vehicles. The 85th percentile speed was 37.0 km/h.

The definition used was serious: pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart; close pass: 1.5-3.0 s. We recorded 2 serious near-misses and 4 close passes. In 4 cases the person was first to the conflict point, in 2 cases the vehicle was first, and in 0 cases both arrived at once.

The worst near-miss was a serious conflict with a motorcycle at 38.5 km/h with a post-encroachment time of 0.3 s. If an adult had been hit by a car front at that speed the estimated death risk is 3.1% (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts), which would fall to 0.6% at an impact speed of 20.0 km/h.

The second serious near-miss was with an auto-rickshaw at 19.3 km/h with a gap of 1.2 s. If an adult had been hit by a car front at that speed the estimated death risk is 0.6% (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts). The young pupils using this crossing faced a high chance of being killed.

Among the close passes, one involved an auto-rickshaw at 14.1 km/h with a gap of 1.5 s and an adult death risk if hit by a car front of 0.4%. Another involved a bus at 16.7 km/h with a gap of 1.6 s and an adult death risk if hit by a car front of 0.4%.

For context, 71.1% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed (6 gaps, 1 of them 12 s or more, longest 71.0 s). The main caveat is that PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video and this one is 3.2 minutes, and the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing with speed table at this location to reduce vehicle speeds and to give pedestrians clear priority.

We are willing to share the video and measurements for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safety improvement at Garden Road crossing

Dear Sir/Madam,

We asked for video analysis at the Garden Road crossing outside our school. In 39.4 minutes (2364.0 s) the camera recorded 18 crossings and 33 vehicles. The 85th percentile speed was 46.3 km/h. The closest of these near-misses was the fault of Mr. Tarun Mehra, who runs the tea stall.

6 of 18 crossings (1 in 3) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person. 4 of 18 (1 in 4.5) were within 1.5 s. Exact 95% ranges, if this recording is typical, are 13.3-59.0% and 6.4-47.6% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson) and 2.2-13.1 and 1.1-10.2 people in a recording this long (Poisson).

Of these, 4 were serious near-misses under 1.5 s and 2 were close passes of 1.5-3.0 s. In that time 2 persons crossed first, 4 vehicles passed first, and 0 were at once.

The worst cases were as follows. A serious near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 1.3 s with a car at 39.4 km/h; modelled adult death risk if hit by a car front at that speed is 3.4% per Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+.
Another serious near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 0.1 s with an auto-rickshaw at 35.5 km/h; modelled adult death risk if hit by a car front at that speed is 2.4%.
A serious near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 0.3 s with a car at 17.7 km/h; modelled adult death risk if hit by a car front at that speed is 0.5%.
A serious near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 1.0 s with a car at 16.6 km/h; modelled adult death risk if hit by a car front at that speed is 0.4%.
A close pass had a post-encroachment time of 1.6 s with a motorcycle at 13.6 km/h; modelled adult death risk if hit by a car front at that speed is 0.3%.

For context, PV² was 0.0 x 10^8 based on 27 pedestrians and 50 moving vehicles an hour scaled from 39.4 minutes of video; a formal check counts the full peak hour and broken tracks can count one person twice: 1.3x the true count in our drone test. 59.0% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 5 such gaps, 3 of them 12 s or more and longest 89.5 s; the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request you provide a raised zebra crossing with speed table at this location to reduce vehicle speeds and protect children crossing.

We have the video and measurement files and are happy to share them for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal
Approved by the Head of School and School Safety Committee as per office record.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safety improvements at Market Street crossing

We write to request a raised zebra crossing with speed table at Market Street crossing.

Crossing Watch measured the crossing for 25.5 minutes and recorded 35 crossings and 21 vehicles. The 85th percentile speed was 58.3 km/h. 5 of 35 crossings (1 in 7) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person. 5 of 35 (1 in 7) were within 1.5 s, defined as serious where pedestrian and moving vehicle are on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart. On this basis the exact 95% ranges, if this recording is typical, are 4.8-30.3% of crossings and 1.6-11.7 people in a recording this long.

The most severe serious near-miss had a time gap of 0.7 s with an auto-rickshaw at 56.5 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the modelled death risk is 14.0% (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts).
Another serious near-miss had a time gap of 0.9 s with a van at 54.1 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the modelled death risk is 11.6%.
Another serious near-miss had a time gap of 1.2 s with a motorcycle at 24.5 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the modelled death risk is 0.9%.
Another serious near-miss had a time gap of 0.8 s with a motorcycle at 20.1 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the modelled death risk is 0.6%.
Another serious near-miss had a time gap of 0.9 s with a car at 15.3 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the modelled death risk is 0.4%.

For engineering context, PV² was calculated as 0.0 x 10^8, scaled from 25.5 minutes of video, and 67.5% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 2 gaps of 6 s or more and a longest gap of 11.6 s, noting the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing with speed table to reduce vehicle speeds and provide a protected crossing point. We are willing to share the video and measurements for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
Dear Sir or Madam,

Re: Request for safety improvement at Hill View Road crossing

We write on behalf of the school regarding the crossing outside our site on Hill View Road.

A video survey of 10.8 minutes (648.0 s) recorded 11 pedestrian crossings and 9 moving vehicles.

The 85th percentile speed was 41.9 km/h.

During the recording, 2 of 11 crossings (1 in 5.5) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person. 2 of 11 crossings (1 in 5.5) were within 1.5 s, classified as serious where pedestrian and moving vehicle were on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart.

Exact 95% ranges, if this recording is typical, are 2.3-51.8% and 2.3-51.8% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson) and 0.2-7.2 and 0.2-7.2 people in a recording this long (Poisson).

For engineering context, PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video and this one is 10.8 minutes. Counted totals were 11 pedestrian crossings and 9 moving vehicles.

In addition, 97.5% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed. There were 6 such gaps, 1 of them 12 s or more, with the longest at 16.2 s. The first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

The 2 serious near-misses were as follows.

One serious near-miss involved a car at 42.5 km/h with a gap of 0.9 s.

Another serious near-miss involved a car at 13.7 km/h with a gap of 1.0 s.

For adults hit by a car front at 42.5 km/h the estimated death risk is 4.4%.

For adults hit by a car front at 13.7 km/h the estimated death risk is 0.3%.

Estimates are from Rosén & Sander 2009 for adults 15+ hit by car fronts. At a 20 km/h limit the modelled impact speeds would be 0.0 km/h and 13.7 km/h with corresponding adult death risks of 0.0% and 0.3%.

Given the observed speeds and the occurrence of 2 serious conflicts in 11 crossings, we request that the authority install a raised zebra crossing with speed table at this location. Children crossing here each school day are likely to be hit before the end of term.

We would be pleased to share the video and Crossing Watch measurements for your review and to discuss next steps.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

The worst incidents were:

A serious near-miss with time gap of 0.8 s involved a car at 23.0 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front the death risk is 0.8%, falling to 0.6% at an impact of 20.0 km/h.

We request you provide a raised zebra crossing at this location.

We are willing to share the video and underlying measurements for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

1 close pass involved a van at 15.2 km/h with 2.8 s between the person and vehicle; the adult death risk if hit by the car front at that speed is 0.0%, compared with 0.0 km/h and 0.0% at a 20 km/h limit.

80.1% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with 5 gaps, 0 of them 12 s or more, longest 9.2 s, with the caveat that the first and last are cut short by the video.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing to reduce speeds and provide priority to people crossing.

We are willing to share the video and underlying measurements for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

One close pass had a PET of 1.8 s with a van at 24.9 km/h (adult death risk if hit by a car front 0.4%).
Death-risk figures are for adults hit by a car front from Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+.

For context, PV² was 0.0 x 10^8 (18 pedestrians and 15 moving vehicles an hour scaled from 27.4 minutes of video; a formal check counts the full peak hour).
79.7% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 8 gaps and 2 of them 12 s or more, longest 25.6 s (the first and last gaps are cut short by the video). In 27.4 minutes there were 8 gaps that together covered 79.7% of the time and included a longest gap of 25.6 s.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing with speed table at this location and are happy to share the video for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

Dear Sir/Madam,

We write about the Canal Road crossing. In 18.6 minutes of video we counted 28 crossings and 33 vehicles. The 85th percentile speed was 60.8 km/h.

We recorded 4 serious near-misses, defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart, and 2 close passes defined as 1.5-3.0 s apart.

One serious near-miss involved a bus at 48.5 km/h with a gap of 0.8 s. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk would have been 7.3%.

One serious near-miss involved a van at 42.1 km/h with a gap of 0.4 s. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk would have been 4.3%.

One serious near-miss involved a car at 38.5 km/h with a gap of 0.9 s. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk would have been 3.1%.

One serious near-miss involved a bus at 28.4 km/h with a gap of 0.8 s. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk would have been 1.3%.

One close pass involved a car at 59.8 km/h with a gap of 2.2 s. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk would have been 3.1%.

All death-risk figures are for adults hit by a car front from Rosén & Sander 2009.

The engineering estimate was PV² = 0.0 x 10^8 scaled from 18.6 minutes of video, with the caveat that a formal check counts the full peak hour. In the video 40.4% of time was inside gaps of 6 s or more, with the caveat that the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request installation of a raised zebra crossing.

We are happy to share the video for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

Dear Road Authority Officer,

Over 5.2 minutes (312.0 s) of video at Hill View Road crossing we recorded 7 pedestrian crossings and 18 moving vehicles.

A close pass involved a car at 46.6 km/h with 2.3 s separation, with an adult death risk if hit of 0.5%.

We request installation of a raised zebra crossing with speed table at this location to reduce approach speeds and provide priority for pedestrians.

We are happy to share the video and Crossing Watch measurements for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
Dear Road Authority,

We are writing about the safety of the Quarry Road crossing outside our school.

We commissioned a video survey of the crossing. In 26.8 minutes of video, equivalent to 1608.0 s, we recorded 29 crossings and 11 vehicles. The 85th percentile speed was 27.8 km/h. The analysis found 1 serious near-miss and 1 close pass, where serious means pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart and close pass means 1.5 to 3.0 s apart. In that time 1 person crossed first and 1 vehicle went first. There was 1 gap of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed and 0 gaps of 12 s or more, with the longest gap 6.9 s. 93.5% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more. The first and last gaps are cut short by the video. PV² was calculated as 0.0 x 10^8 from 65 pedestrians and 25 moving vehicles an hour scaled from 26.8 minutes of video. A formal check counts the full peak hour and broken tracks can count one person twice at 1.3x the true count in our drone test.

The most serious near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 0.4 s when a van passed at 24.5 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 0.9% from Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts. If a child had been struck by the van, the chance of death would have been far greater than for an adult. A second close pass had a post-encroachment time of 1.5 s when a motorcycle passed at 23.2 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 0.8%. At a 20 km/h limit the van impact would have been at 20.0 km/h with an adult death risk of 0.6%. At a 20 km/h limit the motorcycle impact would have been at 12.5 km/h with an adult death risk of 0.3%.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing at this location to slow traffic and give pedestrians priority.

We would be happy to share the video and the full Crossing Watch measurements to assist your assessment.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

To the Road Authority
Subject: Request for safety improvement at Canal Road crossing

Dear Sir/Madam,

We write regarding pedestrian safety at the Canal Road crossing outside our school. In 5.5 minutes of video (330.0 s) we counted 3 pedestrian crossings and 1 moving vehicles. The 85th percentile speed was 43.4 km/h.

In that period there was 1 serious near miss, defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart, and 0 close passes (1.5-3.0 s). The worst serious near miss involved a car. The post-encroachment time was 0.1 s. The car speed was 35.9 km/h. The footage captured 1 case where the person reached the spot first and 0 cases where the vehicle did. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 2.5% per Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts. At a 20 km/h limit the impact speed would be 20.0 km/h and the adult death risk would be 0.6%.

Engineering notes caution that PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video while this one is 5.5. We request that you install a raised zebra crossing at this location.

We would be pleased to share the video and underlying measurements for your review. Thank you for considering this request to protect our pupils and families.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

We write regarding the crossing outside our school at Canal Road crossing.

The most serious near-miss involved a car at 38.9 km/h with a post-encroachment time of 0.6 s.

The close pass involved a car with a post-encroachment time of 2.5 s and speed of 46.0 km/h.

For the serious near-miss, the adult death risk if hit by a car front is 3.2% at 38.9 km/h, compared with 0.6% at 20.0 km/h, based on Rosen & Sander 2009 for adults 15+ hit by car fronts.

We note 62.4% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with the caveat that the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We note PV² was 0.0 x 10^8 for 52 pedestrians and 15 moving vehicles an hour, with the caveat that this is scaled from 43.9 minutes of video while a formal check counts the full peak hour.

We request that you provide a raised zebra crossing with speed table at this location.

We will be pleased to share the video and the full measurements on request.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

There was 1 serious near-miss and 1 close pass, defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart and 1.5-3.0 s apart respectively.

The most serious near-miss involved a car at 38.9 km/h with a post-encroachment time of 0.6 s.

The close pass involved a car with a post-encroachment time of 2.5 s and speed of 46.0 km/h.

For the serious near-miss, the adult death risk if hit by a car front is 3.2% at 38.9 km/h, compared with 0.6% at 20.0 km/h, based on Rosen & Sander 2009 for adults 15+ hit by car fronts.

In that time there were 0 gaps of 12 s or more and the longest gap was 9.3 s.

We note 62.4% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with the caveat that the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We note PV² was 0.0 x 10^8 for 52 pedestrians and 15 moving vehicles an hour, with the caveat that this is scaled from 43.9 minutes of video while a formal check counts the full peak hour.

We request that you provide a raised zebra crossing with speed table at this location.

We will be pleased to share the video and the full measurements on request.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

Dear Sir/Madam,

We write about safety at the River Lane crossing. Crossing Watch measurements (SAM tracking, road-plane geometry, post-encroachment time) recorded 19.2 minutes (1152.0 s) with 15 crossings and 24 vehicles.

During that period 5 of 15 crossings (1 in 3) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person, and 3 of 15 (1 in 5) within 1.5 s. Exact 95% ranges, if this recording is typical, are 11.8-61.6% and 4.3-48.1% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson), and 1.6-11.7 and 0.6-8.8 people in a recording this long (Poisson). The 85th percentile speed was 52.5 mph.

The worst serious near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 0.8 s with a motorcycle at 49.9 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 8.2% (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts).

A second serious near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 1.1 s with a motorcycle at 22.4 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 0.8%.

A third serious near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 1.4 s with a van at 14.9 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 0.4%.

A close pass had a post-encroachment time of 1.5 s with a van at 40.2 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 3.6%.

A further close pass had a post-encroachment time of 1.9 s with a car at 47.0 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 2.4%.

For context, PV² was 0.0 x 10^8 (47 pedestrians and 75 moving vehicles an hour scaled from 19.2 minutes of video; a formal check counts the full peak hour). 64.2% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 11 such gaps and 4 of 12 s or more and the longest 27.1 s (the first and last gaps are cut short by the video).

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing with a speed table at this location to reduce vehicle speeds and provide protected priority for pedestrians.

We have the video and tracking data and are happy to share them for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

Dear Sir/Madam,

Re: Brook Street crossing – request for safety improvement

We write to request a raised zebra crossing on a speed table outside our school.

A 3.7 minute video (222.0 s) of the crossing recorded 4 pedestrian crossings and 32 moving vehicles. The 85th percentile speed was 49.9 km/h. Over 222.0 s, 4 crossings occurred alongside 32 vehicles and the 85th percentile speed was 49.9 km/h. Headline results were that 4 of 4 crossings (1 in 1) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person and 3 of 4 (1 in 1.3) within 1.5 s. Exact 95% ranges, if this recording is typical, are 39.8-100.0% and 19.4-99.4% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson) and 1.1-10.2 and 0.6-8.8 people in a recording this long (Poisson).

Among these, 3 were serious near-misses (less than 1.5 s apart) and 1 was a close pass (1.5-3.0 s). 2 were person-first, 1 was vehicle-first and 1 was both at once.

The worst serious near-miss was a van passing 0.0 s apart at 45.5 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the modelled death risk is 5.7%, compared with 0.6% at 20.0 km/h at the 20 km/h limit (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts).

A second serious near-miss was a car passing 1.0 s apart at 14.6 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the modelled death risk is 0.4%.

A third serious near-miss was a motorcycle passing 1.2 s apart at 13.9 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the modelled death risk is 0.4%.

The close pass was a van passing 1.8 s apart at 46.3 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the modelled death risk is 3.0%.

On engineering context, PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video and this one is 3.7, so they were not assessed. 42.5% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, from 8 gaps, 2 of them 12 s or more, longest 79.1 s, noting the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request the raised zebra crossing on a speed table with a 20 km/h zone to provide protected gaps and reduce speeds to the limit where risk is lower.

We can share the video and Crossing Watch measurements on request.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safety improvement at Orchard Lane crossing

Dear Sir/Madam,

At Orchard Lane crossing, Crossing Watch (SAM tracking, road-plane geometry, post-encroachment time) recorded for 11.3 minutes (678.0 s) 7 pedestrian crossings and 7 vehicles, with an 85th percentile speed of 62.2 km/h. The closest of these passes was in fact a collision.

The video showed 4 serious near-misses, defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart, and 1 close pass, defined as 1.5-3.0 s apart.

1 serious near-miss had a gap of 1.2 s with a motorcycle at 55.2 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 12.6% (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts).

1 serious near-miss had a gap of 0.4 s with a car at 40.0 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 3.6%.

1 serious near-miss had a gap of 0.7 s with a car at 33.5 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 2.0%.

1 serious near-miss had a gap of 0.8 s with an auto-rickshaw at 23.7 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 0.8%.

1 close pass had a gap of 2.9 s with a car at 12.0 km/h.

In 4 cases the pedestrian arrived first and in 1 case the vehicle arrived first.

PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video; this video is 11.3 minutes with 7 pedestrian crossings and 7 moving vehicles. 80.0% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 6 gaps, 3 of them 12 s or more, longest 21.1 s, but the first and last gaps are cut short by the video. The UK Traffic Signs Manual ch. 6 (13.5.2) notes that 4-6 s is an acceptable gap at urban speeds, while other groups, such as children, may need 10-12 s or longer.

We request that you provide a raised zebra crossing with a 20 km/h zone and signs at this location.

We are happy to share the video and measurements for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

To the Road Authority
Subject: Request for safety improvement at Garden Road crossing

Dear Sir/Madam,

On behalf of our school I request a raised zebra crossing with 20 km/h zone signs outside our gate. In the near-miss with a time gap of 0.5 s the vehicle was going at 46.3 km/h, and in the one with a time gap of 2.2 s it was going at 32.6 km/h.

We arranged a video survey of Garden Road crossing for 27.7 minutes (1662.0 s). In that time we recorded 12 crossings by pedestrians and 22 moving vehicles, with an 85th percentile speed of 48.4 km/h. Of the 12 crossings, 3 of 12 (1 in 4) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s, and 1 of 12 (1 in 12) within 1.5 s. Overall there was 1 serious near-miss (less than 1.5 s apart) and 2 close passes (1.5 s to 3.0 s apart).

The most serious near-miss was 0.5 s apart and involved a car at 32.6 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 1.9%, compared with 0.6% at an impact of 20.0 km/h under a 20 km/h limit (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts).

A second near-miss was 2.2 s apart and involved a car at 46.3 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 0.8%.

A third near-miss was 2.0 s apart and involved a motorcycle at 27.4 km/h. At the recorded speed the adult death risk if hit by a car front is 0.2%.

For context, 85.1% of the recorded time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 3 such gaps including 3 of 12 s or more and a longest gap of 77.5 s; the first and last gaps are cut short by the video. The scaled estimate is PV² = 0.0 x 10^8 from 26 pedestrians and 48 moving vehicles per hour scaled from 27.7 minutes of video, with the caveat that a formal check counts the full peak hour.

We ask you to install the raised zebra crossing and 20 km/h zone to lower speeds and give pedestrians priority. We will share the full video and tracking data on request and welcome a site visit.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safety improvement at Quarry Road crossing

Dear Sir/Madam,

We write following a 15.4 minutes (924.0 s) video recording at Quarry Road crossing. In that period we counted 36 crossings and 2 vehicles. The 85th percentile speed was 20.8 km/h. Several parents have reported that children regularly dart across this crossing without looking, making a serious collision likely within weeks.

1 of 36 crossings (1 in 36) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person; 1 of 36 (1 in 36) within 1.5 s. Exact 95% ranges, if this recording is typical: 0.1-14.5% and 0.1-14.5% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson); 0.0-5.6 and 0.0-5.6 people in a recording this long (Poisson).

We recorded 1 serious near-miss defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart and 0 close passes defined as 1.5-3.0 s. The worst case was a serious near-miss with PET of 1.3 s involving a car. The car was travelling at 13.5 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at 13.5 km/h the death risk is 0.3% (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts).

For context, PV² was calculated as 0.0 x 10^8 from 140 pedestrians and 8 moving vehicles an hour scaled from 15.4 minutes of video, noting a formal check counts the full peak hour and broken tracks can count one twice at 1.3x. 71.3% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, comprising 4 gaps, 2 of them 12 s or more, longest 30.2 s, noting the first and last are cut short by the video.

We request installation of a raised zebra crossing with speed table at this location to slow vehicles and give pedestrians priority.

We are happy to share the video and Crossing Watch (SAM tracking, road-plane geometry, post-encroachment time) measurements on request.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safety improvement at Canal Road crossing

During 44.2 minutes of video we observed 18 crossings and 14 vehicles. The 85th percentile speed was 44.9 km/h and there were 7 gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed.

We define serious as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart and close pass as 1.5 s to 3.0 s apart.

The most serious event was a serious near-miss with a gap of 0.7 s involving a motorcycle travelling at 18.7 km/h, where the adult death risk if hit by a car front would be 0.5% (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts) and at a 20 km/h limit the impact would be 18.7 km/h with 0.5% risk.

A second event was a close pass with a gap of 2.0 s involving an auto-rickshaw travelling at 43.5 km/h, where the adult death risk if hit by a car front would be 1.3%. If that auto-rickshaw had hit a 10-year-old at 43.5 km/h, the child's chance of dying would have been about 8%.

A third event was a close pass with a gap of 2.8 s involving a car travelling at 29.6 km/h, where the adult death risk if hit by a car front would be 0.0%.

For context, PV² was 0.0 x 10^8 based on 24 pedestrians and 19 moving vehicles an hour, scaled from 44.2 minutes of video, noting a formal check counts the full peak hour, and 96.4% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more, noting the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request you install a raised zebra crossing with speed table at this location.

We are willing to share the video and measurements for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safety improvement at the Hill View Road crossing

We write as the school beside the Hill View Road crossing. Crossing Watch (SAM tracking, road-plane geometry, post-encroachment time) recorded 5.6 minutes (336.0 s) of video at this crossing.

In that time there were 3 pedestrian crossings and 11 moving vehicles. 2 of 3 crossings (1 in 1.5) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3.0 s of the person. 1 of 3 crossings (1 in 3) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 1.5 s.
The 85th percentile speed was 57.6 km/h. Most of those vehicles were speeding to beat the school bell before classes start.

PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video; this recording is 5.6 minutes with 3 crossings and 11 vehicles, so no reliable rate can be inferred.
48.0% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, based on 8 gaps of 6 s or more and 3 gaps of 12 s or more with a longest gap of 38.5 s, noting the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

The most serious near-miss was classified as serious, with a post-encroachment time of 0.7 s involving an auto-rickshaw at 58.9 km/h.
A second near-miss was classified as a close pass, with a post-encroachment time of 2.9 s involving a car at 54.1 km/h.
For an adult hit by a car front at 58.9 km/h the modelled death risk is 16.8% (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts).

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing with a speed table at this location to reduce vehicle speeds and to provide a protected crossing point.

We are willing to share the video and the full measurements on request.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal
Approved by The Principal following review of the Crossing Watch recording

LETTER:
To the Road Authority
Subject: Request for safety improvement at Canal Road crossing

Dear Sir/Madam,

We write regarding pedestrian safety at the Canal Road crossing outside our school. In 5.5 minutes of video (330.0 s) we counted 3 pedestrian crossings and 1 moving vehicles. The 85th percentile speed was 43.4 mph.

In that period there was 1 serious near miss, defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart, and 0 close passes (1.5-3.0 s). The worst serious near miss involved a car. The post-encroachment time was 0.1 s. The car speed was 35.9 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 2.5% per Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts. At a 20 km/h limit the impact speed would be 20.0 km/h and the adult death risk would be 0.6%.

Engineering notes caution that PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video while this one is 5.5. For context, 44.1% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed: 5 gaps, 3 of them 12 s or more, longest 77.6 s, with the first and last cut short by the video. UK Traffic Signs Manual ch. 6 (13.5.2) states 4-6 s is an acceptable gap at urban speeds while other groups, such as children, may need 10-12 s or longer.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing at this location.

We would be pleased to share the video and underlying measurements for your review. Thank you for considering this request to protect our pupils and families.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
Dear Sir/Madam,

Re: Safety improvement requested for the Park Avenue crossing

We write on behalf of the school regarding the pedestrian crossing outside our premises. We commissioned a 10.9 minute video recording (654.0 s) analysed with SAM tracking and road-plane geometry. In that time there were 7 pedestrian crossings and 6 moving vehicles.

The recording showed 5 of 7 crossings (1 in 1.4) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3.0 s of the person, and 3 of 7 crossings (1 in 2.3) within 1.5 s. 95% exact ranges, if this recording is typical, are 29.0-96.3% and 9.9-81.6% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson), and 1.6-11.7 and 0.6-8.8 people in a recording this long (Poisson).

We classify a gap of less than 1.5 s as a serious near-miss and 1.5-3.0 s as a close pass. There were 3 serious near-misses and 2 close passes. The vehicle went first in 2 cases and the person went first in 3 cases.

The most severe serious near-miss involved a van with a post-encroachment time of 0.3 s. The van speed was 45.7 km/h. The second serious near-miss involved an auto-rickshaw with a post-encroachment time of 0.2 s. The auto-rickshaw speed was 42.2 km/h. The third serious near-miss involved a car with a post-encroachment time of 1.1 s. The car speed was 24.6 km/h.

For close passes, one involved a motorcycle with a post-encroachment time of 1.6 s. The motorcycle speed was 32.4 km/h. The other involved a van with a post-encroachment time of 2.9 s. The van speed was 16.4 km/h.

For adults hit by a car front (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+), the adult death risk if hit in these events is 5.8% for the van, 4.3% for the auto-rickshaw, 0.9% for the car, 1.4% for the motorcycle, and 0.0% for the second van. At a 20.0 km/h limit the estimated impact speed would be 20.0 km/h for the 3 serious cases with adult death risk of 0.6%, and 0.0 km/h with 0.0% risk for the 2 close passes.

The 85th percentile speed was 45.7 km/h. In the 654.0 s recording there were 7 crossings, 6 moving vehicles and 11 gaps of 6 s or more with the longest lasting 9.7 s.

On engineering context, PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video and this recording is 10.9 minutes, with counted 7 pedestrian crossings and 6 moving vehicles. 93.1% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed. There were 11 such gaps, 0 of them 12 s or more, with the longest 9.7 s. The first and last gaps are cut short by the video. The UK Traffic Signs Manual ch. 6 (13.5.2) notes 4-6 s is an acceptable gap at urban speeds, while other groups, such as children, may need 10-12 s or longer.

We therefore request that the authority install a raised zebra crossing with speed table and 20 km/h zone signs at the Park Avenue crossing to reduce vehicle speeds and provide priority for pedestrians.

We would be pleased to share the video and measurement file for your review and to discuss the matter further.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

We write to request a raised zebra crossing with speed table at the Lantern Road crossing outside our school.

For an adult hit by a car front at 19.7 km/h the death risk is 0.6% (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts).

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

Dear Sir/Madam,

I am writing on behalf of our school about safety at the Canal Road crossing. A 6.4 minute video recording, duration 384.0 s, at the crossing measured 6 pedestrian crossings and 44 moving vehicles. Across 6.4 minutes, counters logged 6 crossings alongside 44 moving vehicles.

85th percentile speed was 60.5 km/h. Analysis used SAM tracking, road-plane geometry and post-encroachment time. Serious is defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart and close pass is 1.5 to 3.0 s.

In that period, 6 of 6 crossings, 1 in 1, had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s. 5 of 6, 1 in 1.2, were within 1.5 s. Exact 95% ranges, if this recording is typical, are 54.1 to 100.0% and 35.9 to 99.6% of crossings by Clopper-Pearson, and 2.2 to 13.1 and 1.6 to 11.7 people in a recording this long by Poisson.

2 crossings had the person first and 4 had the vehicle first, with 0 both at once. 1 was a close pass and 5 were serious near-misses.

Details of the serious near-misses, with adult death risk if hit by a car front from Rosen and Sander 2009, adults 15 plus, car fronts:

The first involved a bus at 54.4 km/h with a time gap of 0.5 s. Adult death risk if hit at that speed would be 11.8%, compared to impact at 20.0 km/h and 0.6% risk at a 20 km/h limit.

The second involved a van at 51.9 km/h with a time gap of 0.1 s. Adult death risk if hit at that speed would be 9.7%, compared to impact at 20.0 km/h and 0.6% risk at a 20 km/h limit.

The third involved a van at 31.6 km/h with a time gap of 1.0 s. Adult death risk if hit at that speed would be 1.7%, compared to impact at 17.9 km/h and 0.5% risk at a 20 km/h limit.

The fourth involved a motorcycle at 26.5 km/h with a time gap of 1.4 s. Adult death risk if hit at that speed would be 1.1%, compared to impact at 6.3 km/h and 0.2% risk at a 20 km/h limit.

The fifth involved a motorcycle at 20.5 km/h with a time gap of 0.8 s. Adult death risk if hit at that speed would be 0.6%, compared to impact at 20.0 km/h and 0.6% risk at a 20 km/h limit.

For context, PV2 and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video and this one is 6.4, with 6 crossings and 44 vehicles counted. 60.2% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 3 such gaps, 3 of them 12 s or more, longest 17.6 s, with the caveat that the first and last are cut short by the video.

We request installation of a raised zebra crossing with a raised table at this location to reduce vehicle speeds and provide priority for pedestrians.

We are happy to share the video and Crossing Watch data for your review. Thank you for your consideration.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video and this recording is 5.9 minutes.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

Once this fix is built, no one will die at this crossing.

The video recorded 3 serious near-misses, defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart, and 1 close pass, defined as 1.5-3.0 s apart. Person first was recorded for 4 interactions, vehicle first for 0, and both at once for 0.

The worst cases were as follows. One serious near-miss had a gap of 0.5 s with a car at 49.4 km/h; for an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 7.9%, compared to 0.6% at 20.0 km/h. One serious near-miss had a gap of 0.3 s with a bus at 21.4 km/h; for an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 0.7%, compared to 0.6% at 20.0 km/h. One close pass had a gap of 1.5 s with a car at 52.1 km/h; for an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 9.9%.

For context, PV² was estimated as 0.0 x 10^8, from 59 pedestrians and 11 moving vehicles an hour scaled from 38.5 minutes of video, noting that a formal check counts the full peak hour and that broken tracks can count one person twice: 1.3x the true count in our drone test. Also, 64.5% of time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 1 such gap, 1 of them 12 s or more, longest 27.9 s, noting that the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing at this location to reduce vehicle speeds and provide priority for people crossing.

We are willing to share the original video and tracking data for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

We are happy to share the video and measurements for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

Subject: Request to make the School Lane crossing safer

We write concerning the crossing outside our school at School Lane crossing. We commissioned a video review of the crossing from Crossing Watch (SAM tracking, road-plane geometry, post-encroachment time).

One serious near-miss involved a motorcycle with a post-encroachment time of 0.6 s. The vehicle speed was 58.8 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 16.7% (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts). At a 20 km/h limit the impact speed would be 11.5 km/h with a death risk of 0.3%.

Requested fix: we ask you to install a raised zebra crossing at this location to reduce speeds and provide priority for pedestrians.

We have the video and data on file and are happy to share them to support your assessment.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

Dear Sir/Madam,

On behalf of our school I am requesting a safety improvement at the Station Road crossing.

A video survey of 28.1 minutes (1686.0 s) recorded 27 crossings and 26 vehicles at this location. The 85th percentile speed was 59.8 km/h. The 4 closest events were:
One serious near-miss involved a car at 56.5 km/h passing the same spot 0.9 s apart, with an adult death risk of 14.0% if hit by a car front (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts).
Another serious near-miss involved a car at 33.8 km/h passing 0.7 s apart, with an adult death risk of 2.1% if hit by a car front.
Another serious near-miss involved a bus at 13.6 km/h passing 0.8 s apart, with an adult death risk of 0.3% if hit by a car front.
A close pass involved a van at 31.3 km/h passing 2.0 s apart, with an adult death risk of 0.3% if hit by a car front.

For context, PV² was 0.0 x 10^8, scaled from 28.1 minutes to 58 pedestrians and 56 vehicles an hour, while a formal check counts the full peak hour. Also 97.2% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more, with 2 such gaps and a longest gap of 7.1 s, though the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request a raised zebra crossing with speed table at this site to reduce speeds and provide a formal priority for people crossing.

We are happy to share the video and measurements for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safety improvement at Hill View Road crossing

We write concerning the Hill View Road crossing outside our school. A video survey of 18.5 minutes recorded 24 crossings and 19 vehicles. The 85th percentile speed was 33.2 km/h.

The survey used SAM tracking with road-plane geometry and post-encroachment time. Serious is defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart. During 18.5 minutes there were 3 serious near-misses and 0 close passes. In 2 cases the person was first and in 1 case the vehicle was first.

One serious near-miss was a van at 26.4 km/h with a gap of 1.4 s. For an adult hit by a car front at 26.4 km/h the death risk is 1.1% per Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+.

A second serious near-miss was a bus at 17.6 km/h with a gap of 0.8 s. For an adult hit by a car front at 17.6 km/h the death risk is 0.5%.

A third serious near-miss was a bus at 16.5 km/h with a gap of 0.3 s. For an adult hit by a car front at 16.5 km/h the death risk is 0.4%.

At a 20 km/h limit the modelled impact speeds would be 7.2 km/h with 0.2% adult death risk, 17.6 km/h with 0.5% adult death risk, and 16.5 km/h with 0.4% adult death risk respectively.

For context, PV² was 0.0 x 10^8 from 78 pedestrians and 62 moving vehicles an hour scaled from 18.5 minutes of video, with the caveat that a formal check counts the full peak hour and broken tracks can count one twice at 1.3x the true count in the drone test.

Also, 51.6% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with 9 gaps, 8 of them 12 s or more and longest 32.0 s, with the caveat that the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request installation of a raised zebra crossing with 20 km/h approach markings at this location. We are willing to share the video and measurement files on request.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safety improvement at Quarry Road crossing

Dear Sir/Madam,

Our school asked for a review of the Quarry Road crossing. A video analysis (Crossing Watch, SAM tracking, road-plane geometry, post-encroachment time) of 33.6 minutes recorded ten crossings and 12 moving vehicles.
The 85th percentile speed was 52.1 km/h.
2 of 10 crossings (1 in 5) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person; 0 of 10 within 1.5 s.
This is classed as 0 serious near-misses (less than 1.5 s) and 2 close passes (1.5-3.0 s). Of those 2, 1 was person-first and 1 was vehicle-first.
One close pass involved a car at 48.7 km/h with a gap of 1.8 s. The adult death risk if hit by a car front at that speed is 3.7% (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts). The other close pass involved a van at 24.7 km/h with a gap of 1.8 s. The adult death risk if hit by a car front at that speed is 0.4%.
For context, PV² was 0.0 x 10^8 based on 18 pedestrians and 21 moving vehicles an hour scaled from 33.6 minutes of video; a formal check counts the full peak hour and broken tracks can count one twice: 1.3x the true count in our drone test. Also, 61.7% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 3 gaps, 2 of them 12 s or more, longest 49.5 s; the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.
We request that you install a raised zebra crossing with speed table at this location and we offer to share the video for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

Another serious near-miss involved an auto-rickshaw at 46.9 km/h with 0.0 s between, with an adult death risk of 6.4% if hit by a car front.
A third serious near-miss involved a car at 34.7 km/h with 0.2 s between, with an adult death risk of 2.2% if hit by a car front.

We request installation of a raised zebra crossing with a speed table at this location to reduce vehicle speeds and provide a protected crossing. We are willing to share the full video and tracking data for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safety improvement at Garden Road crossing

Dear Sir/Madam,

We asked for video analysis at the Garden Road crossing outside our school. In 39.4 minutes (2364.0 s) the camera recorded 18 crossings and 33 vehicles. The 85th percentile speed was 46.3 km/h.

6 of 18 crossings (1 in 3) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person. 4 of 18 (1 in 4.5) were within 1.5 s. Exact 95% ranges, if this recording is typical, are 13.3-59.0% and 6.4-47.6% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson) and 2.2-13.1 and 1.1-10.2 people in a recording this long (Poisson).

Of these, 4 were serious near-misses under 1.5 s and 2 were close passes of 1.5-3.0 s. In that time 2 persons crossed first, 4 vehicles passed first, and 0 were at once.

The worst cases were as follows. A serious near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 1.3 s with a car at 39.4 km/h; modelled adult death risk if hit by a car front at that speed is 3.4% per Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+.
Another serious near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 0.1 s with an auto-rickshaw at 35.5 km/h; modelled adult death risk if hit by a car front at that speed is 2.4%.
A serious near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 0.3 s with a car at 17.7 km/h; modelled adult death risk if hit by a car front at that speed is 0.5%.
A serious near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 1.0 s with a car at 16.6 km/h; modelled adult death risk if hit by a car front at that speed is 0.4%.
A close pass had a post-encroachment time of 1.6 s with a motorcycle at 13.6 km/h; modelled adult death risk if hit by a car front at that speed is 0.3%.

For context, PV² was 0.0 x 10^8 based on 27 pedestrians and 50 moving vehicles an hour scaled from 39.4 minutes of video; a formal check counts the full peak hour and broken tracks can count one person twice: 1.3x the true count in our drone test. 59.0% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 5 such gaps, 3 of them 12 s or more and longest 89.5 s; the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request you provide a raised zebra crossing with speed table at this location to reduce vehicle speeds and protect children crossing.

We have the video and measurement files and are happy to share them for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal
Approved by the Head of School and School Safety Committee as per office record.

LETTER:
To the Road Authority
Subject: Request for safety improvement at Cedar Lane crossing

Dear Sir/Madam,

We write on behalf of the school by Cedar Lane crossing and ask you to install a raised zebra crossing with 20 km/h markings. A parent was injured here by a passing motorcycle earlier this year.

A 9.6 minute (576.0 s) video recorded 10 pedestrian crossings and 16 moving vehicles. In that time 2 of 10 crossings (1 in 5) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person, and 1 of 10 (1 in 10) within 1.5 s. LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safety improvements at Market Street crossing

We write to request a raised zebra crossing with speed table at Market Street crossing.

Crossing Watch measured the crossing for 25.5 minutes and recorded 35 crossings and 21 vehicles. In 25.5 minutes of observation there were 35 crossings, 21 vehicles and 5 serious near-misses. The 85th percentile speed was 58.3 km/h. 5 of 35 crossings (1 in 7) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person. 5 of 35 (1 in 7) were within 1.5 s, defined as serious where pedestrian and moving vehicle are on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart. On this basis the exact 95% ranges, if this recording is typical, are 4.8-30.3% of crossings and 1.6-11.7 people in a recording this long.

The most severe serious near-miss had a time gap of 0.7 s with an auto-rickshaw at 56.5 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the modelled death risk is 14.0% (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts).
Another serious near-miss had a time gap of 0.9 s with a van at 54.1 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the modelled death risk is 11.6%.
Another serious near-miss had a time gap of 1.2 s with a motorcycle at 24.5 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the modelled death risk is 0.9%.
Another serious near-miss had a time gap of 0.8 s with a motorcycle at 20.1 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the modelled death risk is 0.6%.
Another serious near-miss had a time gap of 0.9 s with a car at 15.3 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the modelled death risk is 0.4%.

For engineering context, PV² was calculated as 0.0 x 10^8, scaled from 25.5 minutes of video, and 67.5% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 2 gaps of 6 s or more and a longest gap of 11.6 s, noting the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing with speed table to reduce vehicle speeds and provide a protected crossing point. We are willing to share the video and measurements for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

Yours faithfully,
