LETTER:
Dear Sir/Madam,

Re: Brook Street crossing – request for safety improvement

We write to request a raised zebra crossing on a speed table outside our school.

A 3.7 minute video (222.0 s) of the crossing recorded 4 pedestrian crossings and 32 moving vehicles. The 85th percentile speed was 49.9 km/h. Headline results were that 4 of 4 crossings (1 in 1) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person and 3 of 4 (1 in 1.3) within 1.5 s. Exact 95% ranges, if this recording is typical, are 39.8-100.0% and 19.4-99.4% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson) and 1.1-10.2 and 0.6-8.8 people in a recording this long (Poisson).

Among these, 3 were serious near-misses (less than 1.5 s apart) and 1 was a close pass (1.5-3.0 s). 2 were person-first, 1 was vehicle-first and 1 was both at once.

The worst serious near-miss was a van passing 0.0 s apart at 45.5 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the modelled death risk is 5.7%, compared with 0.6% at 20.0 km/h at the 20 km/h limit (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts).

A second serious near-miss was a car passing 1.0 s apart at 14.6 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the modelled death risk is 0.4%.

A third serious near-miss was a motorcycle passing 1.2 s apart at 13.9 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the modelled death risk is 0.4%.

The close pass was a van passing 1.8 s apart at 46.3 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the modelled death risk is 3.0%.

On engineering context, PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video and this one is 3.7, so they were not assessed. 42.5% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, from 8 gaps, 2 of them 12 s or more, longest 79.1 s, noting the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request the raised zebra crossing on a speed table with a 20 km/h zone to provide protected gaps and reduce speeds to the limit where risk is lower. Without intervention, a child is likely to be killed here within the next year.

We can share the video and Crossing Watch measurements on request.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safer crossing at Quarry Road crossing

We write as the head of the school adjoining the Quarry Road crossing. We commissioned a video review of the crossing covering 20.5 minutes, during which 17 crossings and 16 vehicles were observed.

Of the 17 crossings, 5 of 17 (1 in 3.4) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3.0 s of the person and 2 of 17 (1 in 8.5) within 1.5 s. The exact 95% ranges, if this recording is typical, are 10.3-56.0% and 1.5-36.4% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson) and 1.6-11.7 and 0.2-7.2 people in a recording this long (Poisson). In total there were 2 serious near-misses defined as less than 1.5 s apart and 3 close passes defined as 1.5-3.0 s apart.

The worst events were as follows. One serious near-miss had a gap of 0.0 s between a van travelling at 41.7 km/h and a person at the same spot. A parent was injured here by a passing motorcycle earlier this year. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 4.1% under Rosén & Sander 2009, and it would be 0.6% if impact were at 20.0 km/h.

A second serious near-miss had a gap of 0.8 s between a car travelling at 18.7 km/h and a person. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 0.5%.

A close pass had a gap of 2.6 s involving a car travelling at 59.8 km/h. A close pass had a gap of 2.4 s involving a bus travelling at 15.8 km/h. A close pass had a gap of 2.6 s involving a motorcycle travelling at 28.8 km/h.

Engineering context from the same video is limited. PV² was 0.0 x 10^8 based on 50 pedestrians and 47 moving vehicles per hour scaled from 20.5 minutes of video, with the caveat that a formal check counts the full peak hour. 68.5% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with the caveat that the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request that you provide a raised zebra crossing with a speed table at this location to reduce vehicle speeds and to give pedestrians priority.

We are willing to share the video and the full measurements for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safety improvements at Hill View Road crossing

We write regarding pedestrian safety outside our school at Hill View Road crossing.

Crossing Watch recorded 19 crossings and 12 vehicles in 44.5 minutes. 2 of 19 crossings (1 in 9.5) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person and 2 of 19 (1 in 9.5) within 1.5 s. LETTER:
To the Road Authority
Subject: Request for safety improvements at Quarry Road crossing

We write to request a raised zebra crossing with speed table at Quarry Road crossing.

A Crossing Watch video review (SAM tracking, road-plane geometry, post-encroachment time) monitored the crossing for 34.7 minutes (2082.0 s). In that time 22 people crossed and 21 vehicles passed. The 85th percentile speed was 55.3 km/h. Had a child been struck, the impact would almost certainly have been fatal.

The review defined serious as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart and close pass as 1.5-3.0 s. It found 2 serious near-misses and 4 close passes. Person first was 3 and vehicle first was 3.

One serious near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 1.0 s with a van travelling at 54.5 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at 54.5 km/h the death risk is 12.0% (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts).

A second serious near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 0.3 s with an auto-rickshaw travelling at 29.4 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at 29.4 km/h the death risk is 1.4%.

A close pass had a post-encroachment time of 1.8 s with a van travelling at 56.1 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at 56.1 km/h the death risk is 7.0%.

Engineering review noted PV² = 0.0 x 10^8 from 38 pedestrians and 36 moving vehicles an hour scaled from 34.7 minutes of video. Its main caveat is that a formal check counts the full peak hour and broken tracks can count one twice: 1.3x the true count in our drone test.

The review also noted 51.1% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 1 gap of 6 s or more and a longest gap of 11.1 s. Its main caveat is that the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing with speed table at this location to reduce vehicle speeds and provide a protected crossing for school children and staff.

We are willing to share the full video and Crossing Watch measurements for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

I write about safety at Mill Street crossing following video measurements made by Crossing Watch (SAM tracking, road-plane geometry, post-encroachment time).

The second event was a close pass with a post-encroachment time of 1.5 s with a van travelling at 28.9 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 1.3%, and at a 20 km/h limit the impact would be 0.0 km/h with a death risk of 0.0%.

Also 63.9% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed: 1 gap, 0 of them 12 s or more, longest 6.9 s, with the first and last gaps cut short by the video.

We request installation of a raised zebra crossing with speed table at this location to reduce vehicle speeds and provide priority for pedestrians.

We can share the video and measurements on request and would welcome a site meeting.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

We write about the Park Avenue crossing outside our school. In 9.5 minutes of video we counted 7 pedestrian crossings and 14 moving vehicles. The 85th percentile speed was 43.9 km/h.

By definition, a serious near-miss is pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart and a close pass is 1.5-3.0 s apart. We recorded 2 serious near-misses and 2 close passes.

In 3 cases the pedestrian was first and in 1 case the vehicle was first.

Engineering note: 59.9% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed. There was 1 gap of 6 s or more and 1 gap of 12 s or more, with the longest gap 48.8 s. PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video and this one is 9.5 minutes, and the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing at this location to reduce vehicle speeds and give priority to people crossing.

We can share the full video and measurements for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

Dear Sir/Madam,

We are writing about the Orchard Lane crossing. Crossing Watch analysis (SAM tracking, road-plane geometry, post-encroachment time) of 8.5 minutes (510.0 s) counted 3 pedestrian crossings and 8 moving vehicles, with an 85th percentile speed of 31.6 km/h. These near-misses happened because drivers ignored the crossing markings.

There was 1 serious near-miss (pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart) and 2 close passes (1.5-3.0 s). The most serious event had a post-encroachment time of 0.2 s with a car travelling at 30.8 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the estimated death risk is 1.6% (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts), falling to 0.6% if impact were at 20.0 km/h.

The next close pass had a post-encroachment time of 2.4 s with a bus travelling at 33.0 km/h.

The remaining close pass had a post-encroachment time of 2.9 s with a van travelling at 31.7 km/h.

Engineering context is limited: PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video and this video is 8.5 minutes. During the observed period 66.7% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 10 such gaps and 4 of them 12 s or more and the longest 44.3 s, noting the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request installation of a raised zebra crossing to reduce vehicle speeds and give priority to pedestrians.

We are willing to share the video and measurements for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safety improvement at the Quarry Road crossing

We write as the school using the Quarry Road crossing. A video survey (Crossing Watch, SAM tracking, road-plane geometry, post-encroachment time) measured the following.

Over 8.4 minutes (504.0 s) we counted 3 pedestrian crossings and 20 moving vehicles. The 85th percentile speed was 64.0 km/h.

3 of 3 crossings (1 in 1) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person; 3 of 3 (1 in 1) within 1.5 s. Exact 95% ranges, if this recording is typical: 29.2-100.0% and 29.2-100.0% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson); 0.6-8.8 and 0.6-8.8 people in a recording this long (Poisson).

We recorded 3 serious near-misses and 0 close passes, where serious means pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart and a close pass is 1.5-3.0 s. In all 3 cases the person reached the conflict point before the vehicle did.

Details of the worst cases:
The most serious near-miss was serious with a PET of 0.2 s involving an auto-rickshaw at 58.4 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front, death risk at 58.4 km/h is 16.2% compared with 0.6% at an impact of 20.0 km/h (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts).
A second serious near-miss had a PET of 0.5 s involving a car at 50.6 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front, death risk at 50.6 km/h is 8.7% compared with 0.6% at an impact of 20.0 km/h.
A third serious near-miss had a PET of 1.1 s involving an auto-rickshaw at 20.0 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front, death risk at 20.0 km/h is 0.6% compared with 0.6% at an impact of 20.0 km/h.

On gaps and engineering context, with their main caveats: PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video; this one is 8.4. Counted: 3 pedestrian crossings, 20 moving vehicles. 56.0% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed: 6 gaps, 5 of them 12 s or more, longest 35.8 s (the first and last are cut short by the video).

We request installation of a raised zebra crossing with speed table and 20 km/h approach signs at this location to lower vehicle speeds toward 20.0 km/h and protect pedestrians.

We are willing to share the video and measurement files for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
Dear Road Authority,

We are writing about the safety of the Quarry Road crossing outside our school.

We commissioned a video survey of the crossing. In 26.8 minutes of video, equivalent to 1608.0 s, we recorded 29 crossings and 11 vehicles. The 85th percentile speed was 27.8 km/h. The analysis found 1 serious near-miss and 1 close pass, where serious means pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart and close pass means 1.5 to 3.0 s apart. In that time 1 person crossed first and 1 vehicle went first. There was 1 gap of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed and 0 gaps of 12 s or more, with the longest gap 6.9 s. 93.5% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more. The first and last gaps are cut short by the video. PV² was calculated as 0.0 x 10^8 from 65 pedestrians and 25 moving vehicles an hour scaled from 26.8 minutes of video. A formal check counts the full peak hour and broken tracks can count one person twice at 1.3x the true count in our drone test.

The most serious near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 0.4 s when a van passed at 24.5 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 0.9% from Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts. A second close pass had a post-encroachment time of 1.5 s when a motorcycle passed at 23.2 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 0.8%. At a 20 km/h limit the van impact would have been at 20.0 km/h with an adult death risk of 0.6%. At a 20 km/h limit the motorcycle impact would have been at 12.5 km/h with an adult death risk of 0.3%.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing at this location to slow traffic and give pedestrians priority.

We would be happy to share the video and the full Crossing Watch measurements to assist your assessment.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
Dear Sir or Madam,

Re: Request for safety improvement at Hill View Road crossing

We write on behalf of the school regarding the crossing outside our site on Hill View Road.

A video survey of 10.8 minutes (648.0 s) recorded 11 pedestrian crossings and 9 moving vehicles.

The 85th percentile speed was 41.9 mph.

During the recording, 2 of 11 crossings (1 in 5.5) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person. 2 of 11 crossings (1 in 5.5) were within 1.5 s, classified as serious where pedestrian and moving vehicle were on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart.

Exact 95% ranges, if this recording is typical, are 2.3-51.8% and 2.3-51.8% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson) and 0.2-7.2 and 0.2-7.2 people in a recording this long (Poisson).

For engineering context, PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video and this one is 10.8 minutes. Counted totals were 11 pedestrian crossings and 9 moving vehicles.

In addition, 97.5% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed. There were 6 such gaps, 1 of them 12 s or more, with the longest at 16.2 s. The first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

The 2 serious near-misses were as follows.

One serious near-miss involved a car at 42.5 km/h with a gap of 0.9 s.

Another serious near-miss involved a car at 13.7 km/h with a gap of 1.0 s.

For adults hit by a car front at 42.5 km/h the estimated death risk is 4.4%.

For adults hit by a car front at 13.7 km/h the estimated death risk is 0.3%.

Estimates are from Rosén & Sander 2009 for adults 15+ hit by car fronts. At a 20 km/h limit the modelled impact speeds would be 0.0 km/h and 13.7 km/h with corresponding adult death risks of 0.0% and 0.3%.

Given the observed speeds and the occurrence of 2 serious conflicts in 11 crossings, we request that the authority install a raised zebra crossing with speed table at this location.

We would be pleased to share the video and Crossing Watch measurements for your review and to discuss next steps.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
Dear Sir/Madam,

We are writing about safety at the Market Street crossing outside our school. A video survey of 16.0 minutes (960.0 s) recorded 3 crossings and 13 vehicles.

Across those 3 crossings, 2 of 3 crossings (1 in 1.5) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person, and 1 of 3 (1 in 3) within 1.5 s.

The most serious near-miss involved a van at 29.0 km/h with a post-encroachment time of 0.9 s. The closest of these passes was in fact a collision. The estimated adult death risk if hit by a car front at that speed is 1.3% (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts). A second close pass involved a car at 32.2 km/h with 1.8 s gap. Its estimated adult death risk if hit is 0.8%.

The 85th percentile speed was 33.4 km/h. PV² was 0.0 x 10^8 based on 11 pedestrians and 49 moving vehicles an hour scaled from 16.0 minutes of video, noting a formal check counts the full peak hour. Also, 57.1% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 10 gaps, 5 of them 12 s or more, longest 52.1 s, noting the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing with speed table at this location to reduce vehicle speeds and provide priority for people crossing.

We would be pleased to share the video and measurements for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
Dear Sir/Madam,

We write concerning the School Lane crossing. A video recording of 37.9 minutes (2274.0 s) was analysed with SAM tracking and road-plane geometry. In that time 6 people crossed and 11 vehicles passed. The 85th percentile speed was 43.5 km/h. A parent was injured here by a passing motorcycle earlier this year.

The analysis found 5 of 6 crossings (1 in 1.2) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3.0 s of the person. 4 of 6 crossings (1 in 1.5) were within 1.5 s. Exact 95% ranges, if this recording is typical, are 35.9% to 99.6% and 22.3% to 95.7% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson), and 1.6 to 11.7 and 1.1 to 10.2 people in a recording this long (Poisson).

By definition a serious near-miss is less than 1.5 s apart and a close pass is 1.5 s to 3.0 s apart, measured as post-encroachment time. There were 4 serious near-misses and 1 close pass. The person crossed first in 4 cases and the vehicle first in 1 case.

The worst events were:
A bus at 36.4 km/h was 0.9 s from the person. The adult death risk if hit by a car front at that speed is 2.6% (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+), falling to 0.4% at an impact of 16.1 km/h under a 20 km/h limit.
A car at 32.7 km/h was 0.5 s from the person. The adult death risk if hit by a car front at that speed is 1.9%, falling to 0.6% at an impact of 20.0 km/h under a 20 km/h limit.
A car at 20.9 km/h was 0.6 s from the person. The adult death risk if hit by a car front at that speed is 0.7%, falling to 0.6% at an impact of 20.0 km/h under a 20 km/h limit.
A motorcycle at 18.7 km/h was 0.2 s from the person. The adult death risk if hit by a car front at that speed is 0.5%, remaining 0.5% at an impact of 18.7 km/h under a 20 km/h limit.
A bus at 14.0 km/h was 1.8 s from the person. The adult death risk if hit by a car front at that speed is 0.0%, remaining 0.0% at an impact of 0.0 km/h under a 20 km/h limit.

Engineering context with caveats: PV² was 0.0 x 10^8 based on 9 pedestrians and 17 moving vehicles per hour scaled from 37.9 minutes, with the caveat that a formal check counts the full peak hour and that broken tracks can count one person twice (1.3x the true count in drone test). 41.8% of time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 2 gaps of 6 s or more and 1 gap of 12 s or more and a longest gap of 17.1 s, with the caveat that the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing with speed table and 20 km/h zone signs at this location to reduce speeds and provide priority for people crossing.

We can share the video and measurements on request.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safety improvements at Market Street crossing

We write to request a raised zebra crossing with speed table at Market Street crossing.

Crossing Watch measured the crossing for 25.5 minutes and recorded 35 crossings and 21 vehicles. The 85th percentile speed was 58.3 km/h. The van that came closest is driven by Mr. Ashok Varghese of the corner shop. 5 of 35 crossings (1 in 7) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person. 5 of 35 (1 in 7) were within 1.5 s, defined as serious where pedestrian and moving vehicle are on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart. On this basis the exact 95% ranges, if this recording is typical, are 4.8-30.3% of crossings and 1.6-11.7 people in a recording this long.

The most severe serious near-miss had a time gap of 0.7 s with an auto-rickshaw at 56.5 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the modelled death risk is 14.0% (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts).
Another serious near-miss had a time gap of 0.9 s with a van at 54.1 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the modelled death risk is 11.6%.
Another serious near-miss had a time gap of 1.2 s with a motorcycle at 24.5 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the modelled death risk is 0.9%.
Another serious near-miss had a time gap of 0.8 s with a motorcycle at 20.1 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the modelled death risk is 0.6%.
Another serious near-miss had a time gap of 0.9 s with a car at 15.3 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the modelled death risk is 0.4%.

For engineering context, PV² was calculated as 0.0 x 10^8, scaled from 25.5 minutes of video, and 67.5% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 2 gaps of 6 s or more and a longest gap of 11.6 s, noting the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing with speed table to reduce vehicle speeds and provide a protected crossing point. We are willing to share the video and measurements for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safety improvement at Bridge Street crossing

We write concerning the Bridge Street crossing outside our school. A video review using SAM tracking and road-plane geometry measured 28.5 minutes (1710.0 s) of activity, with 25 crossings and 8 vehicles. The 85th percentile speed was 13.9 km/h.

In that period there were 0 serious near misses and 1 close pass. 1 of 25 crossings had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s, and 0 of 25 within 1.5 s. The exact 95% ranges, if this recording is typical, are 0.1-20.4% and 0.0-13.7% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson) and 0.0-5.6 and 0.0-3.7 people in a recording this long (Poisson).

The worst event was a close pass with a gap of 2.6 s. The vehicle was a car travelling at 12.2 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed, Rosén & Sander 2009 estimates 0.0% death risk. Children hit at these speeds would face a 12% risk of dying. At a 20 km/h limit the impact speed would be 0.0 km/h with 0.0% death risk for an adult hit by a car front.

For context, PV² was 0.0 x 10^8 based on 53 pedestrians and 17 vehicles an hour scaled from 28.5 minutes of video, while a formal check counts the full peak hour. Also 50.9% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, from 10 gaps including 3 of 12 s or more and a longest gap of 84.6 s, noting the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request you install a raised zebra crossing at this location to slow traffic and protect children crossing to school.

We can share the full video and tracking data on request and welcome a site visit to discuss the findings.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
Dear Sir/Madam,

We write about the Bridge Street crossing outside our school.

Measurements were made from 42.4 minutes of video, a duration of 2544.0 s, using Crossing Watch with SAM tracking, road-plane geometry and post-encroachment time. In that period 15 crossings and 17 vehicles were recorded. The 85th percentile speed was 57.2 km/h. Most drivers here were exceeding the posted 30 km/h speed limit.

A serious near-miss is defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart; a close pass is 1.5 s to 3.0 s apart. There was 1 serious near-miss and 3 close passes.

The most serious event had a gap of 0.8 s between a van travelling at 53.1 km/h and a pedestrian, with an adult death risk if hit by a car front of 10.7% from Rosén & Sander 2009 for adults 15+.

A second event was a close pass with a gap of 1.8 s involving a car travelling at 41.9 km/h, with an adult death risk of 2.0%.

A third event was a close pass with a gap of 2.4 s involving a bus travelling at 49.4 km/h, with an adult death risk of 0.4%.

A fourth event was a close pass with a gap of 2.1 s involving a motorcycle travelling at 25.6 km/h, with an adult death risk of 0.0%.

For context, PV² was 0.0 x 10^8, calculated as 21 pedestrians and 24 moving vehicles an hour scaled from 42.4 minutes of video, with the caveat that a formal check counts the full peak hour and broken tracks can count one person twice at 1.3x the true count in our drone test.

43.7% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 3 gaps of 6 s or more and 1 gap of 12 s or more and a longest gap of 72.0 s, with the caveat that the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing with speed table at this location to reduce vehicle speeds and provide a safe place to cross.

We have the video and tracking data available and are happy to share it with you for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
Dear Sir/Madam,

We are writing about the Quarry Road crossing outside our school.

In 41.4 minutes of video (2484.0 s) we recorded 5 crossings and 16 vehicles.

4 of 5 crossings (1 in 1.2) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person.

3 of 5 crossings (1 in 1.7) were within 1.5 s.

Exact 95% ranges, if this recording is typical, are 28.4-99.5% and 14.7-94.7% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson) and 1.1-10.2 and 0.6-8.8 people in a recording this long (Poisson).

We recorded 3 serious near-misses defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart and 1 close pass defined as 1.5-3.0 s.

The 85th percentile speed was 56.8 km/h. One near-miss ended with the vehicle hitting the person crossing.

1 serious near-miss involved an auto-rickshaw at 58.3 km/h with a PET of 1.0 s. The modelled death risk for an adult hit by a car front at that speed is 16.1% (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts).

Another serious near-miss involved a car at 25.6 km/h with a PET of 0.1 s. The modelled death risk for an adult hit by a car front at that speed is 1.0%.

A 3rd serious near-miss involved a car at 20.4 km/h with a PET of 0.4 s. The modelled death risk for an adult hit by a car front at that speed is 0.6%.

An additional close pass involved a van at 24.1 km/h with a PET of 2.6 s. The modelled death risk for an adult hit by a car front at that speed is 0.0%.

For context, PV² was 0.0 x 10^8 for 7 pedestrians and 23 moving vehicles an hour scaled from 41.4 minutes of video, noting a formal check counts the full peak hour and broken tracks can count one twice by 1.3x in our drone test.

66.5% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 3 gaps, 0 of them 12 s or more and longest 7.0 s, noting the first and last are cut short by the video.

We request a raised zebra crossing with speed table and 20 km/h zone signs at this location.

We would be pleased to share the video for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safety improvement at Lantern Road crossing

We write about the Lantern Road crossing outside our school. Measurements from 41.7 minutes of video, 2502.0 s in total, recorded 28 crossings and 10 vehicles, with an 85th percentile speed of 45.0 km/h. In the near-miss with a time gap of 1.3 s the vehicle was going at 43.9 km/h, and in the one with a time gap of 1.8 s it was going at 40.3 km/h.

In that recording, 4 of 28 crossings had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3.0 s, and 1 of 28 within 1.5 s. There was 1 serious near-miss defined as less than 1.5 s and 3 close passes defined as 1.5 to 3.0 s. In 2 cases the person was first and in 2 cases the vehicle was first, with 0 cases at once.

The most serious near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 1.3 s and involved a motorcycle at 40.3 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the estimated death risk is 3.6 percent from Rosén and Sander 2009, adults 15 plus, car fronts.

A second near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 1.8 s and involved a car at 43.9 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the estimated death risk is 2.4 percent from the same source.

A third near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 1.9 s and involved a car at 44.4 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the estimated death risk is 1.9 percent from the same source.

A fourth near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 1.7 s and involved a car at 12.7 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the estimated death risk is 0.2 percent from the same source.

For context, PV2 was 0.0 x 10 to the 8, calculated as 40 pedestrians and 14 moving vehicles an hour scaled from 41.7 minutes of video, noting a formal check counts the full peak hour and that broken tracks can count one pedestrian twice as 1.3 times the true count in drone testing. Also 40.7 percent of time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 7 gaps of 6 s or more, 4 of them 12 s or more, longest 24.5 s, noting the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request installation of a raised zebra crossing with speed table at Lantern Road crossing to give pedestrians priority and reduce vehicle speeds.

We are willing to share the video and Crossing Watch tracking data for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Dear Sir/Madam,

We write about pedestrian safety at the Park Avenue crossing outside our school.

A 3.7 minute video (222.0 s) recorded 10 pedestrian crossings and 43 moving vehicles. The 85th-percentile speed was 59.1 km/h. There were 5 serious near-misses, defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart, and 1 close pass of 1.5-3.0 s. Of the 6 close interactions, 3 were person first and 3 were vehicle first and 0 were both at once.

The worst near-misses were:
One serious near-miss involved a bus at 55.6 km/h with 1.3 s between road users and an adult death risk if hit of 13.1%.
One serious near-miss involved a motorcycle at 47.1 km/h with 0.8 s between road users and an adult death risk if hit of 6.5%.
One serious near-miss involved a car at 41.5 km/h with 1.4 s between road users and an adult death risk if hit of 4.1%.
One serious near-miss involved a car at 34.4 km/h with 1.3 s between road users and an adult death risk if hit of 2.2%.
One serious near-miss involved an auto-rickshaw at 30.9 km/h with 0.7 s between road users and an adult death risk if hit of 1.6%.
Death-risk figures are for adults hit by a car front from Rosen & Sander 2009, adults 15+.

In that video PV2 and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video and this one is 3.7 minutes. Also, 90.6% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more, with 6 gaps and 0 of them 12 s or more and longest 10.5 s, with the first and last gaps cut short by the video.

We request installation of a raised zebra crossing with a speed table to slow traffic and provide priority for pedestrians.

We are happy to share the video and Crossing Watch data for your review and would welcome a site visit.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal
Approved by The Principal

LETTER:
Dear Road Authority,

I write about safety at the Cedar Lane crossing outside our school.

In 23.0 minutes of video we recorded 22 crossings and 18 vehicles, with 85th percentile speed 33.0 km/h. With this measure in place there will be no more fatalities here.

3 of 22 crossings (1 in 7.3) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person, including 1 of 22 (1 in 22) within 1.5 s.

By definition serious means less than 1.5 s apart and close pass means 1.5-3.0 s apart.

The most serious case was 0.3 s apart involving a car at 35.1 km/h.

If an adult had been hit by a car front at that speed the modelled death risk was 2.3%, compared with 0.6% at 20.0 km/h impact from Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts.

A close pass was 1.5 s apart involving a bus at 12.8 km/h.

A close pass was 2.6 s apart involving a car at 35.2 km/h.

In 3 cases the vehicle went through before the person.

Dear Sir or Madam,

Re: Request for safety improvement at Hill View Road crossing

We write on behalf of the school regarding the crossing outside our site on Hill View Road.

A video survey of 10.8 minutes (648.0 s) recorded 11 pedestrian crossings and 9 moving vehicles.

The 85th percentile speed was 41.9 km/h. The recording captured 9 vehicles over 648.0 s with 6 gaps of at least 6 s.

During the recording, 2 of 11 crossings (1 in 5.5) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person. 2 of 11 crossings (1 in 5.5) were within 1.5 s, classified as serious where pedestrian and moving vehicle were on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart.

Exact 95% ranges, if this recording is typical, are 2.3-51.8% and 2.3-51.8% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson) and 0.2-7.2 and 0.2-7.2 people in a recording this long (Poisson).

In addition, 97.5% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed. There were 6 such gaps, 1 of them 12 s or more, with the longest at 16.2 s. The first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

The 2 serious near-misses were as follows.

One serious near-miss involved a car at 42.5 km/h with a gap of 0.9 s.

Another serious near-miss involved a car at 13.7 km/h with a gap of 1.0 s.

For adults hit by a car front at 42.5 km/h the estimated death risk is 4.4%.

For adults hit by a car front at 13.7 km/h the estimated death risk is 0.3%.

Estimates are from Rosén & Sander 2009 for adults 15+ hit by car fronts. At a 20 km/h limit the modelled impact speeds would be 0.0 km/h and 13.7 km/h with corresponding adult death risks of 0.0% and 0.3%.

Given the observed speeds and the occurrence of 2 serious conflicts in 11 crossings, we request that the authority install a raised zebra crossing with speed table at this location.

We would be pleased to share the video and Crossing Watch measurements for your review and to discuss next steps.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

We are willing to share the video and the measurements with your engineers and to meet on site.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

One close pass involved a bus at 50.9 km/h with a gap of 2.4 s; adult death risk if hit by a car front at that speed is 0.5%, compared to 0.0% at an impact of 0.0 km/h if limited to 20 km/h.

Another close pass involved a car at 12.1 km/h with a gap of 1.7 s; adult death risk if hit by a car front at that speed is 0.2%, compared to 0.2% at an impact of 5.0 km/h if limited to 20 km/h.

Risk figures are from Rosén & Sander 2009 for adults 15+ hit by car fronts.

We can share the video and Crossing Watch measurements on request.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

Dear Sir/Madam,

We write about the Park Avenue crossing outside our school. Crossing Watch video analysis (SAM tracking, road-plane geometry, post-encroachment time) measured 12 pedestrian crossings and 12 moving vehicles in 10.4 minutes and 624.0 s of video.

Of 12 crossings, 4 of 12 (1 in 3) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person. 1 of 12 (1 in 12) was within 1.5 s. Exact 95% ranges, if this recording is typical, are 9.9-65.1% and 0.2-38.5% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson) and 1.1-10.2 and 0.0-5.6 people in a recording this long (Poisson).

The worst event was classed as serious. The gap was 1.3 s. The vehicle was a car travelling at 53.4 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 11.0% (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts).

A second event was a close pass. The gap was 2.4 s. The vehicle was a car travelling at 54.3 km/h.

A third event was a close pass. The gap was 2.1 s. The vehicle was a car travelling at 12.5 km/h.

A fourth event was a close pass. The gap was 2.7 s. The vehicle was a motorcycle travelling at 52.4 km/h.

For context on exposure, PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video and this one is 10.4. Counted were 12 pedestrian crossings and 12 moving vehicles. 87.3% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed.

We request you install a raised zebra crossing with speed table at this crossing to reduce vehicle speeds and provide protected priority for children and staff crossing.

We can share the video and the full measurements for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal
